policies.title: Brazilian nationals: outside the foreign VIVIS regime
policies.summary: The QGRV governs entry of foreigners; a Brazilian national is therefore outside its foreign visitor-visa classification.
conditions: This citizenship classification does not establish the document requirements for a particular Brazilian national, dual national, carrier, or border route.
It does not determine treatment when a dual national presents a different country's ordinary passport.

policies.title: QGRV-listed ordinary passports: VIVIS visa exemption
policies.summary: For these ordinary national passports, the QGRV VIVIS column records a visa dispensation for a short visitor stay. China is handled by the later country-specific MRE update.
conditions: The QGRV legend limits this policy to the VIVIS column for holders of ordinary passports. PADIP (diplomatic) and PASOF (official or service) columns are separate and are not normalized here.

The precise dispensation period is the numbered VIVIS entry and applicable footnote in the QGRV, rather than a single uniform duration; the table uses 30-, 60-, 90-, 180-, and other specified periods.
A QGRV # marker permits entry with a civil identity card for the marked nationality. This passport classification neither requires nor generalizes that separate identity-card facility.
This policy does not cover a laissez-passer, refugee or alien travel document, diplomatic, official, service, public-affairs, temporary, or other special passport/document.

Visa dispensation is not a residence authorization and does not authorize paid work. VIVIS is limited to visitor purposes; a different purpose, a longer stay, or residence requires the applicable immigration route.

Admission and the authorized stay remain subject to Brazilian border control and all current entry requirements. Any extension is a separate Polícia Federal process and depends on the applicable QGRV reciprocity rule.

policies.title: China ordinary passports: VIVIS visa exemption
policies.summary: MRE's current Zurich consular guidance says Chinese ordinary passport holders have been exempt from VIVIS since 11 May 2026 for the specified short-visit purposes.
conditions: The MRE guidance limits the exemption to multiple-entry tourism, business, transit, artistic, or sports visits, for at most 30 days in one year.
Longer stays and other purposes require the appropriate physical visa under the MRE guidance.

This applies to an ordinary Chinese passport; it does not establish treatment of a PRC Travel Document, Hong Kong SAR passport, Macao SAR passport, Taiwan passport, diplomatic passport, official passport, or another special document.
The consular page's country-specific online filing note does not establish a nationality-wide eVisa category for this normalized visitor classification.

policies.title: Australia, Canada, and United States ordinary passports: electronic VIVIS
policies.summary: Australia, Canada, and United States nationals require a Brazilian visitor visa from 10 April 2025 but may obtain the nationally described electronic visitor visa.
conditions: The MRE source describes this as a visitor visa (VIVIS), not visa-free entry; it is valid only for the visitor purposes and periods the visa grants.
The electronic route is expressly described by MRE for these three nationalities. Generic online consular processing for other nationalities is not normalized as eVisa.
This policy is limited to ordinary national passports and does not establish a rule for diplomatic, official, service, emergency, refugee, alien, or other special travel documents.
A visitor visa does not establish residence or permission for paid employment; entry and admission remain subject to Brazilian immigration control.

application.label: Brazil electronic visitor visa application
steps: Use the MRE-linked electronic visitor-visa application site.
Complete the visitor-visa application and provide the requested supporting documents.
Receive the electronic visa before travel and present it with the ordinary passport used for the application.

policies.title: QGRV-listed ordinary passports: VIVIS required
policies.summary: For these ordinary national passports, the QGRV VIVIS column records that a Brazilian visitor visa is required before the short visit.
conditions: This is limited to the QGRV VIVIS column for an ordinary passport. It does not infer a rule from PADIP, PASOF, residence status, special passport, laissez-passer, refugee document, or alien travel document.
The required visa is a visitor visa; purpose, length, and entry conditions are assessed under the visa and ordinary migration rules, and the visa does not itself authorize residence or paid work.
For Haitian nationals, the later MRE notice says QGRV was updated to require prior consultation with MRE Brasília for VIVIS. That additional case-management condition remains applicable.
For Taiwan, the QGRV's distinct treatment is document-specific; this ISO-code policy does not establish admission on a Taiwan diplomatic, official, or special passport.

policies.title: Mexican nationals: outside foreign visitor visa scope
policies.summary: INM's nationality lists regulate foreign nationals' visitor admission, not Mexican citizens.
conditions: This citizenship classification does not establish document requirements for an individual Mexican national, dual national, carrier, or border route.
It does not determine treatment when a dual Mexican national presents another country's ordinary passport.

policies.title: INM-listed ordinary passports: visitor visa exemption
policies.summary: The listed nationalities may seek admission as visitors without permission to undertake remunerated activities without obtaining a Mexican visa in advance.
conditions: This policy is for a visitor without permission to undertake remunerated activities, including tourism; it does not grant residence, work authorization, or a right to admission.

INM may verify passport or internationally valid identity-and-travel document, travel purpose, accommodation or itinerary, means of subsistence, departure transport, and other relevant information at migration review.
The visitor period is not a guaranteed 180 days: INM authorizes the period at entry, and the visa-required guidance says the non-resident visitor route may not exceed 180 days.
For a land entry, INM requires the applicable completed FMM; international-airport FMM handling is generated through migration control.

This normalization is limited to ordinary national passports. It does not establish rules for residence cards, diplomatic or official documents, refugees, stateless persons, alien travel documents, or other special documents.

policies.title: Russia, Türkiye, and Ukraine: SAE electronic authorization for air visitors
policies.summary: Russian, Turkish, and Ukrainian ordinary passport holders may obtain the SAE pre-travel electronic authorization to fly to Mexico as non-remunerated visitors, instead of first obtaining a Mexican visa.
conditions: SAE is an air-only pre-travel authorization for a visitor without permission for remunerated activities; travel by land or sea requires a Mexican visa under INM's current SAE guidance.

The traveller needs a valid passport, an approved authorization, a participating airline, and a printed authorization for airline and migration checks. Approval does not guarantee admission or the period authorized at entry.

The INM central SAE page says the authorization is valid for 30 days and one entry. A current Mexican consular post in Milan instead states 180 days and one entry; the validity conflict is recorded here and the central INM statement is used operationally pending clarification.

A valid visa of Canada, Japan, the United States, the United Kingdom, or a Schengen country, or permanent residence in the listed countries (including Chile, Colombia, and Peru), is a separate alternative to both Mexican visa and SAE for a visa-required national.
This policy does not establish residence, remunerated activity, ordinary visa-free entry, or a rule for diplomatic, official, emergency, refugee, or other special travel documents.

application.label: INM Sistema de Autorización Electrónica
steps: Complete the INM electronic-authorization request with the valid ordinary passport.
Print the approved authorization before presenting at the participating airline's check-in counter.
Present the authorization and passport for Mexican migration inspection on arrival by air.

policies.title: Brazil: electronic visa for air visitors
policies.summary: From 5 February 2026, Brazilian ordinary passport holders may use Mexico's electronic visitor-visa route for a non-remunerated stay of less than 180 days when entering exclusively by air.
conditions: Mexico's Rio consular guidance calls this route a visa electrónica. It is normalized as eVisa rather than ETA because approval produces a visa and the official application charges a visa fee.
The route is exclusively by air, for fewer than 180 days and without remunerated activities. It is valid for one entry; the Rio source states 180 days' authorization validity.
A Brazilian transit traveller using this route must obtain a new electronic visa each time the traveller disembarks at a Mexican airport.
A residence visa, multiple-entry visa, ten-year visa, land or sea entry, remunerated activity, or other purpose requires the applicable separate Mexican process.
Electronic authorization does not guarantee admission; Mexican migration authorities decide admission and the authorized visitor period at the point of entry.

application.label: Mexico electronic visa application for Brazilian travellers
steps: Complete the electronic visa form using the details from the valid Brazilian passport.
Upload the required face photograph and passport data-page image, then pay the application fee.
Receive the electronic visa before travel and present it with the same passport for the air journey and migration inspection.

policies.title: INM-listed ordinary passports: visitor visa required
policies.summary: The listed nationalities require a Mexican visa for travel as a non-remunerated visitor unless the traveller holds a specifically listed alternative document or qualifies for another documented exception.
conditions: INM says the listed nationalities must obtain the visa corresponding to their condition of stay at a Mexican consulate; for tourism, business, or other non-remunerated activity this is visitor without permission for remunerated activities.

A valid and current visa of Canada, Japan, the United States, the United Kingdom, or a Schengen country is an alternative to a Mexican visa. Permanent residence in Canada, the United States, Japan, the United Kingdom, a Schengen country, Chile, Colombia, or Peru is another alternative.

An ABTC approved by Mexico is an alternative only for air entry and business travel. Aircraft crew certification and a seafarer's book for qualifying crew are separate document-specific alternatives; an air-arriving seafarer also needs proof of enrolment, vessel data, and the Mexican port.

These alternatives do not create nationality-wide visa-free status and do not establish residence, paid work, or admission. The ordinary visitor stay cannot exceed 180 days absent residence or a migration process.
This policy concerns ordinary national passports only. It does not establish a rule for diplomatic, official, emergency, refugee, alien, or other special travel documents.

policies.title: Swiss SEM short-stay visa exemption for listed national passports
policies.summary: SEM List 1 marks each listed nationality as not requiring a visa for a stay of up to 90 days.
conditions: Ordinary/national passport scope only; the SEM table's document and V1 annotations remain controlling.
Short stays only: the table column is for stays of up to 90 days; longer stays are separately marked visa-required.
Does not classify diplomatic, service, official, special, refugee, crew, transit, residence, work, or case-specific exceptions.

policies.title: Swiss SEM Nauru short-stay visa requirement
policies.summary: SEM List 1 marks Nauru as visa-required for stays of up to 90 days.
conditions: Ordinary/national passport scope only, subject to the SEM table's travel-document annotations.
Short stays only: this is the up-to-90-day column, not transit or a long-stay residence decision.
Does not override diplomatic, service, official, special, crew, residence, family, humanitarian, or case-specific exceptions.

policies.title: Norwegian statutory Annex 5 visa-free-state list
policies.summary: Annex 5 expressly lists the named states as visa-free for entry to Norway.
conditions: Applies only to nationals on the current statutory visa-free-state list, whose stated reference date is 14 August 2025.
The Immigration Act limits the total Schengen stay for visa-exempt entrants to three months in six months.
Does not classify diplomatic, service, official, special, crew, transit, residence, asylum, work, document, or case-specific exceptions.

policies.title: Norwegian statutory Nauru visa requirement
policies.summary: Nauru is absent from the complete statutory visa-free-state list, while the Immigration Act imposes a visa requirement unless regulations except it.
conditions: Ordinary-passport nationality result derived from the current complete Annex 5 list and the Act's default visa rule.
The Act separately exempts holders of qualifying Schengen residence permits and recognizes valid Schengen visas.
Does not override diplomatic, service, official, special, crew, transit, asylum, work, document, family, or case-specific exceptions.

policies.title: Liechtenstein's SEM-referred short-stay visa treatment for listed national passports
policies.summary: Liechtenstein's competent authority directs visa-requirement checks to Swiss SEM and states that the two countries generally share entry regulations.
conditions: The Liechtenstein authority expressly directs visa-requirement enquiries to SEM; SEM List 1 marks these national passports visa-free up to 90 days.
Liechtenstein states its rules are generally/largely the same and reserves bilateral or multilateral deviations; this policy is therefore not unconditional.
Does not classify diplomatic, service, official, special, crew, transit, residence, work, family, document, territorial, or case-specific exceptions.

policies.title: Liechtenstein's SEM-referred Nauru short-stay visa treatment
policies.summary: Liechtenstein's competent authority directs visa-requirement checks to Swiss SEM, whose List 1 marks Nauru visa-required up to 90 days.
conditions: The Liechtenstein authority expressly directs visa-requirement enquiries to SEM; SEM List 1 marks Nauru visa-required up to 90 days.
Liechtenstein states its rules are generally/largely the same and reserves bilateral or multilateral deviations; this policy is therefore not unconditional.
Does not override diplomatic, service, official, special, crew, transit, residence, work, family, document, territorial, or case-specific exceptions.

policies.title: EU visa-list Regulation: Nauru exemption remains conditional on a future agreement
policies.summary: The current Regulation lists Nauru in Annex II with a footnote that makes an exemption conditional on entry into force of an agreement still to be concluded with the EU.
conditions: Ordinary-passport short-stay result only, for stays of no more than 90 days in any 180-day period.
The result follows the current Nauru Annex II footnote; it is not a conclusion about a future agreement or its possible effective date.
Article 6 permits Member State exceptions for specified categories, including diplomatic, service, special, crew, school, refugee, and paid-activity cases; those are out of scope.
Does not determine transit, residence, family-free-movement, territorial, document, asylum, humanitarian, or case-specific entry treatment.

policies.title: Fijian nationals: outside foreign visitor visa scope
policies.summary: Fiji Immigration says Fijian passport holders do not need a visa to enter Fiji; they are outside the foreign ordinary-passport visitor classification.
conditions: This citizenship classification does not establish the document requirements for a particular Fijian national, dual national, carrier, or border route.
It does not determine treatment when a dual Fijian national presents another country's ordinary passport.

policies.title: Listed ordinary passports: Fiji visa exemption with Visitor Permit on arrival
policies.summary: Holders of the listed ordinary national passports are exempt from obtaining a Fiji visa before travel and may be issued a Visitor Permit on immigration clearance if entry requirements are met.
conditions: Visa exemption is not a visa on arrival. Fiji Immigration calls the document issued at immigration clearance a Visitor Permit; it is issued on arrival only if entry requirements are met.

For the ordinary visitor route, Fiji Immigration describes holiday, recreational activity, visiting relatives or friends, conferences or meetings, and onward transit among the stated visitor purposes. A Visitor Permit cannot be used to seek employment or work.

The Visitor Permit period may range from several days up to four months. A holiday visitor may seek one extension of up to two months before expiry; the stated exceptions to extension include business visitor permits and students or relatives on 30-day visitor permits.

At clearance, travellers must meet current requirements including a valid foreign passport, return ticket, completed Arrival Card, confirmed Fiji address, sufficient funds, and any required fees. Fiji immigration officers retain admission and permit-period discretion.

Medical-treatment visitors and yacht owners or carrier crew must apply for their permits before arrival. This policy does not establish residence, employment, diplomatic, official, special-document, refugee, or alien-travel-document treatment.

Transit is separate: Fiji Immigration says a traveller transiting Fiji to another destination within 72 hours after entry needs a transit visa before arrival, with onward ticket and final-destination approval evidence.

policies.title: Unlisted ordinary passports: Fiji pre-entry visa required
policies.summary: Fiji Immigration's complete-list default requires these unlisted ordinary national passport holders to obtain a Fiji visa before travelling; a Visitor Permit may then be issued at arrival if entry requirements are met.
conditions: The official default is supported by Fiji Immigration's complete visa-exempt list and its express statement that all countries not on that list must apply for a visa. The visa must be approved before travel; it is a pre-entry authority, not a guarantee of admission.

Non-exempt applicants need the relevant visa before purchasing a ticket and boarding. Fiji Immigration lists sufficient funds, confirmed return ticket and accommodation among current requirements, and may require further verification documents.
A visitor permit on arrival remains distinct from the required visa and is issued only if entry requirements are satisfied. Visitor employment is prohibited.

Transit, medical treatment, yacht ownership, carrier crew, joining a vessel, residence, work, diplomatic, official, refugee, alien, emergency, and other special-document situations require their applicable separate process. For transit applications, Fiji Immigration requires proof of visa or permit for the final destination.
This policy does not establish an electronic visa, visa on arrival, or a nationality-wide exemption based on a third-country visa or residence document.

policies.title: South Africa: 30-day ordinary-passport visa exemption
policies.summary: DHA's current exemption schedule marks these ordinary national passports exempt for 30 days.
conditions: Ordinary national passport holders only, for bona fide holiday or business visits, and only for the 30-day period listed by DHA.
The list is subject to change without notice and individual visa exemption can be officially withdrawn, requiring a port-of-entry visa application.
This does not classify diplomatic, official, service, special, laissez-passer, crew, military, transit, residence, work, accreditation, document, purpose, admissibility, or case-specific exceptions.

policies.title: South Africa: 90-day ordinary-passport visa exemption
policies.summary: DHA's current exemption schedule marks these ordinary national passports exempt for 90 days.
conditions: Ordinary national passport holders only, for bona fide holiday or business visits, and only for the 90-day period listed by DHA.
The list is subject to change without notice and individual visa exemption can be officially withdrawn, requiring a port-of-entry visa application.
This does not classify diplomatic, official, service, special, laissez-passer, crew, military, transit, residence, work, accreditation, document, purpose, admissibility, or case-specific exceptions.

policies.title: South Africa: annual/calendar-year ordinary-passport visa exemption
policies.summary: DHA's current exemption schedule marks these ordinary national passports exempt for up to 90 days per annum or calendar year.
conditions: DHA marks these ordinary passports 90 Days P/A, defined in the schedule as per annum or per calendar year; this is not an unrestricted 90-day-per-visit rule.
For Angola, DHA additionally says each visit may not exceed 30 days.
This does not classify diplomatic, official, service, special, laissez-passer, crew, military, transit, residence, work, accreditation, document, purpose, admissibility, or case-specific exceptions.

policies.title: South Africa: ordinary-passport eVisa availability
policies.summary: These non-exempt ordinary-passport nationalities are on DHA's current eVisa-availability list.
conditions: Only for nationalities named by DHA's current eVisa availability page and not separately exempt under the current DHA exemption schedule.
An eVisa is still a prior visa: it is an electronic alternative to a paper visa, not visa-free admission or a visa on arrival.
Does not classify diplomatic, official, service, special, laissez-passer, crew, military, transit, residence, work, accreditation, document, purpose, admissibility, or case-specific exceptions.

application.label: DHA ePermits eVisa application
steps: Confirm the passport nationality appears in DHA's current eVisa availability list.
Create a DHA ePermits profile and complete the visa application before travel.

policies.title: South Africa: ordinary-passport port-of-entry visa required
policies.summary: The official visa baseline requires a valid visa for foreign nationals other than current exemption-list holders; DHA's eVisa list does not include these nationalities.
conditions: Ordinary national passports only, for a short visit; this is the current default where the nationality is not on DHA's complete ordinary-passport exemption schedule or current eVisa availability list.
A visa authorizes travel to a port of entry but admission remains subject to immigration examination and all document, purpose, funds, onward-travel, health, and admissibility requirements.

Does not override diplomatic, official, service, special, laissez-passer, crew, military, transit, residence, family, humanitarian, waiver, work, accreditation, document, territorial, or case-specific treatment.

policies.title: Named ordinary passports: no advance Bahamas visitor visa
policies.summary: The Bahamas MOFA currently lists these named nationalities and territories as not needing a visa to enter The Bahamas.
conditions: This policy maps only unambiguous current-country entries from MOFA’s list. It does not map the list’s separate territorial or historic labels to another passport code.

For HK, this represents only the page’s named Hong Kong entry; it does not establish treatment for a PRC passport, Hong Kong Certificate of Identity, British National (Overseas), residence document, or another special document.
The page does not give a visa-free visit period for this list. It does not establish employment, residence, study, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, or special-document access.
Admission remains subject to border inspection. The Immigration Act permits an immigration officer to require a passport, visa, nationality/identity document, or permission-to-enter document.
The separate Indian third-country visa or residence exception is deliberately modelled in its own conditional policy.

policies.title: Named ordinary passports: Bahamas Electronic Entry Visa visitor route
policies.summary: The listed nationalities require a Bahamas visa; MOFA provides the official Electronic Entry Visa application route for ordinary visitor visas, subject to its stated conditions.
conditions: The MOFA list expressly identifies these nationalities as needing a visa. India is included only for Indian nationals outside the separately stated third-country visa or permanent-residence exception.
An Electronic Entry Visa is not a guarantee of entry. Visa applicants need a passport with more than six months remaining, and the border officer may deny entry.
Visa-required travellers also need a visa when arriving by cruise ship from the United States. The policy does not establish a transit or cruise exception.
This ordinary visitor route is for leisure (self-sponsored or sponsored). Seaman’s visas are a distinct crew/trade route, and official and diplomatic visas are not available for online application.
Single-entry validity is three months. Multiple-entry visas have separate eligibility and stated three-month, six-month, or one-year periods; the page says three-year visas are not available online.

The ordinary visitor must apply through the official portal, complete the application, provide the stated supporting documents, pay if requested, and present the passport used to apply plus the Electronic Entry Visa on arrival.

application.label: Bahamas Electronic Entry Visa application
application.processingTime: 7–10 business days when supporting documents are in order and no interview is required.
steps: Select the visitor-visa type and submit the online application with passport, photograph, and country-specific supporting documents.
Pay the requested fee and attend an interview or provide additional documents if directed by the Visa Office.
Present the passport used for the application and the approved Electronic Entry Visa to Immigration on arrival.

policies.title: India ordinary passport: third-country visa or permanent-residence exception
policies.summary: An Indian national with a valid Schengen, UK, Canadian, or US visa, or permanent residence in one of those jurisdictions, does not need a Bahamas visa when presenting the stated evidence.
conditions: The traveller must present the qualifying valid third-country visa with the valid passport, or proof of qualifying permanent-resident status with the valid passport, to Bahamas Immigration.
All other Indian nationals require a Bahamas visa and are within the separate Electronic Entry Visa policy.
The page separately exempts Indian diplomatic and official passports; that non-ordinary document exception is not classified here.
This exception does not establish work, residence, crew, transit, diplomatic, official, or unconditional visa-free access, and entry remains subject to border inspection.

policies.title: Mauritius: listed national passports with no visa required
policies.summary: The current PIO country table expressly labels these nationalities 'No visa required'.
conditions: Ordinary/nationality result only: the country table does not establish diplomatic, official, service, special, laissez-passer, refugee, stateless, or other travel-document treatment.

A no-visa classification is not guaranteed admission. Every entrant still needs a recognized passport or travel document, return ticket, re-entry eligibility, funds, and confirmed accommodation or sponsorship.
No gainful activity without a valid residence permit. Residence/work, transit, crew, medical, social/religious, marriage, study, and case-specific entry rules remain separate.

policies.title: Mauritius: listed national passports with a 60-day visa on arrival
policies.summary: The current PIO country table expressly provides a visa for sixty days on arrival to these nationalities.
conditions: Ordinary/nationality result only, for the table's stated 60-day visa-on-arrival period; the Immigration Officer determines admission and the length of any particular visit.
Taiwan is a special document case: its passport is generally listed as unrecognized, but PIO specifically says Taiwan passport holders may receive a 60-day visa on arrival.
Every entrant must meet the current passport/document, return-ticket, re-entry, funds, and accommodation/sponsorship requirements; no gainful activity is permitted without a residence permit.
Does not classify diplomatic, official, service, special, laissez-passer, refugee, stateless, residence, work, crew, transit, medical, social/religious, marriage, study, or case-specific exceptions.

policies.title: Mauritius: listed national passports with a two-week visa on arrival
policies.summary: The current PIO country table expressly provides a visa for two weeks on arrival to these nationalities.
conditions: Ordinary/nationality result only, for the table's stated two-week visa-on-arrival period; it does not establish a 60-day entitlement.
The Immigration Officer makes the final admission decision and decides the length of a particular visit after examination at entry.
Every entrant must meet the current passport/document, return-ticket, re-entry, funds, and accommodation/sponsorship requirements; no gainful activity is permitted without a residence permit.
Does not classify diplomatic, official, service, special, laissez-passer, refugee, stateless, residence, work, crew, transit, medical, social/religious, marriage, study, or case-specific exceptions.

policies.title: Mauritius: listed national passports requiring a visa before travel
policies.summary: The current PIO table requires a visa before travel for these nationalities, and PIO separately gives the same rule for Guyana.
conditions: Ordinary/nationality result only. Apply through a Mauritian diplomatic or consular representative, Air Mauritius where applicable, or PIO's stated fallback channel; wait for the decision before travel.
PIO's current published routes are consular/representative, Air Mauritius office, or the stated email fallback. No nationality-wide electronic-visa route is established by the reviewed sources.

A visa permits travel to a port of entry but does not guarantee admission; all passport/document, purpose, return-ticket, re-entry, funds, accommodation, and immigration-examination requirements still apply.
Does not override diplomatic, official, service, special, laissez-passer, refugee, stateless, residence, work, crew, transit, medical, social/religious, marriage, study, or case-specific exceptions.

application.label: Mauritius PIO visa application instructions
application.processingTime: As far as practicable, 12 working days after complete submission.
steps: Apply through the stated Mauritian diplomatic/consular, Air Mauritius, or PIO fallback route.
Submit the completed form, passport copy, travel, funds, accommodation, residence, and purpose documents required for the case.
Wait for the application outcome before travelling to Mauritius.

policies.title: Malaysian nationals: outside foreign visitor visa scope
policies.summary: Malaysia's foreign visitor-visa and eVisa framework does not classify Malaysian citizens as foreign visa applicants.
conditions: This citizenship classification does not establish the document requirements for a particular Malaysian national, dual national, carrier, or border route.
It does not determine treatment when a dual Malaysian national presents another country's ordinary passport.

policies.title: Ordinary passports outside Malaysia's current visa-required framework: visa-free social visit
policies.summary: The listed ordinary passports are outside the Immigration Department's current visa-required/eVisa nationality framework for a short social visit and are normalized as visa-free visitors.
conditions: This conclusion is limited to an ordinary-passport social visit. The Immigration Department's country table, MYVISA's specified 31-nationality eVisa framework, and the current Ministry of Foreign Affairs country-by-country visa chart together identify the exhaustive ordinary-passport framework; it is not a rule for work, study, residence, media, diplomatic, official, emergency, refugee, laissez-passer, certificate-of-identity, or other special travel documents.

Visa-free duration is nationality- and purpose-specific. This policy does not convert ASEAN arrangements, Taiwan's separate stay limit, or other shorter social-visit permissions into a uniform duration.

MDAC is a separate arrival declaration, not a visa, eVisa, ETA, entry permit, or admission guarantee. Subject to current listed exceptions, submit it within three days including the arrival date and present it with the passport to immigration.

Malaysia determines individual admissibility and issues the appropriate pass at immigration control. A person prohibited under section 8 may be refused despite a valid travel document, visa, ticket, and funds.

Social/business visits are distinct from other pass types, which must generally be applied for before entry. The visitor may not take unauthorised employment, attend school, or undertake other activity outside the authorized pass.

policies.title: China and Myanmar ordinary passports: current special social-visit exemptions
policies.summary: Malaysia's current official guidance separately exempts Chinese and Myanmar ordinary passports from the otherwise visa-required/eVisa social-visit framework, subject to their stated nationality-specific periods and conditions.
conditions: Chinese citizens holding an ordinary passport valid for at least six months are exempt for social visits of up to 30 days per entry for tourism, business, or family visit, with no more than 90 days in any 180-day period. The source excludes a Chinese multiple-entry-visa route from that exemption.
Myanmar ordinary passport holders travelling for a social visit are visa-free for up to 14 days from 1 October 2025 under the current MYVISA FAQ.

These are ordinary-passport social-visit rules, not a rule for diplomatic, official, public-affairs, residence, work, study, long-term, transit, or special travel-document routes. MDAC remains a separate arrival declaration and admission remains discretionary.

policies.title: Indian ordinary passports: temporary social-visit exemption through 31 December 2026
policies.summary: Malaysia's current official guidance temporarily exempts Indian ordinary-passport holders from the otherwise visa-required/eVisa social-visit framework through 31 December 2026.
conditions: The social-visit single-entry exemption is expressly temporary through 31 December 2026. It does not establish an exemption for a different purpose or period after that date.

This is an ordinary-passport social-visit rule, not a rule for diplomatic, official, public-affairs, residence, work, study, long-term, transit, or special travel-document routes. MDAC remains a separate arrival declaration and admission remains discretionary.

policies.title: Listed ordinary passports: Malaysia social-visit eVisa
policies.summary: For the listed ordinary passport nationalities, Malaysia's current MYVISA framework requires a pre-travel eVisa for a social visit, rather than treating the online application as an ETA or ordinary visa-free entry.
conditions: MYVISA identifies eVisa as an electronic visa, not an ETA, and says the single-entry social-visit eVisa is compulsory for the specified nationalities. It is only for social visits such as tourism, family visits, or short business trips.

The ordinary eVisa single-entry route must be obtained before travel. MYVISA says a single-entry eVisa permits one journey within six months of issue, subject to passport validity; neither eVisa nor MDAC guarantees entry.
Afghan ordinary passport holders must first obtain VDR approval before applying for eVisa. The source's diplomatic and official passport exception is not represented by this ordinary-passport policy.

For the specifically named African nationalities in MYVISA's air-only list, entry with eVisa is limited to air entry points. This does not create a general air-only rule for every nationality in this policy.

MDAC remains a separate arrival declaration. Work, study, residence, media, professional/temporary employment, medical treatment and other VDR purposes follow separate advance procedures and are not granted by this social-visit eVisa.

application.label: MYVISA Malaysia eVisa
steps: Apply through the MYVISA official portal before travelling for the eligible social visit.
For Afghanistan, obtain the required VDR approval before the eVisa application.
Present the approved eVisa, passport, MDAC, and supporting entry documents for Malaysian immigration assessment.

policies.title: Israel and North Korea ordinary passports: special advance visa handling
policies.summary: Israeli and North Korean ordinary passports are not within Malaysia's online eVisa application availability and require the applicable special advance visa/approval handling.
conditions: Malaysia's official eVisa guidance excludes applications from Israel and North Korea. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs current chart identifies Israel as requiring KDN (Ministry of Home Affairs) handling; do not infer ordinary visa-free entry or a self-service eVisa route.

The exact advance approval, travel-document acceptance, mission availability, purpose, duration, and admission conditions must be confirmed with Malaysian Immigration or the competent Malaysian mission before travel. The source does not establish a visa-on-arrival or ETA route.

This policy is limited to ordinary passport codes and does not establish diplomatic, official, residence, work, study, transit, refugee, alien-document, laissez-passer, certificate-of-identity, or other special-document treatment. MDAC is separate from visa/approval and does not establish entry permission.

policies.title: MOFA-listed ordinary passports: no Barbados entry visa
policies.summary: The current Barbados foreign-ministry table marks these named foreign nationalities as not requiring a visa to enter Barbados.
conditions: This policy maps only clear current-country rows from the Ministry table. The table’s China entry includes Macau and Hong Kong; CN, HK, and MO are limited to that stated combined entry and do not establish other PRC, Hong Kong, or Macao travel documents.

The table gives different maximum stays by nationality or agreement. No common duration is inferred; the traveller must meet the applicable named-row terms and any current Immigration admission requirements.
This does not establish a route for work, residence, study, crew, diplomatic, official, service, emergency, refugee, stateless, laissez-passer, territory-specific, or other special documents.

All visitors need the online Immigration and Customs Form available 72 hours before arrival, a passport valid for the trip, a return ticket, intended address, and evidence of personal support. Admission remains for the Immigration Officer.

policies.title: MOFA-listed ordinary passports: advance Barbados entry visa
policies.summary: The listed nationalities require an advance Barbados entry visa. The application is online, but Immigration describes the issued authorization as a letter, so this is not classified as a true eVisa.
conditions: The Ministry’s current foreign-national table marks these nationalities as visa required. The applicant must be granted permission before booking and confirming travel.

Immigration states that the issued visa is a letter accepted at airline check-in and by Barbados Immigration; the fully online application and payment process therefore do not establish an eVisa status.
An entry visa is a prerequisite to seek entry, not a guarantee of admission. Permission to enter is granted only by the Immigration Officer at the port of entry.

The standard single-entry authority is one entry within three months and the stated multiple-entry authority is within six months; application evidence, processing, and endorsements remain subject to the authority’s requirements.

Cruise passengers and crew have limited stated airport-to-vessel, same-vessel, and 12-hour transit exceptions. An overnighting crew member requires a visa, and diplomatic-corp fee treatment does not waive the application.

application.label: Barbados online entry-visa application
application.processingTime: Three weeks under Immigration’s published standard process.
steps: Create an account and complete the online entry-visa application and payment process before travel.
Provide the signed application, photograph, passport biographic-page copy, purpose and support documents, and residence-status evidence where applicable.
Carry the authorization letter and meet the visitor and border-inspection requirements on arrival.

policies.title: Haiti ordinary passport: advance Barbados entry visa unless document exception applies
policies.summary: A regular Haitian passport holder requires an advance Barbados entry visa unless the holder has the stated qualifying permanent-residence or Green Card document.
conditions: The Ministry table says a visa is required for regular Haitian passport holders and directs them to the Immigration online application portal.
The separate qualifying-resident exception and diplomatic/official passport treatment are not part of this standard ordinary-passport policy.
The authorization is an advance entry-visa letter rather than a true eVisa, and it does not guarantee entry. Visitor admission, purpose, transit, crew, and port-inspection rules remain applicable.

application.label: Barbados online entry-visa application
application.processingTime: Three weeks under Immigration’s published standard process.
steps: Submit the online entry-visa application and payment before travel.
Provide the required regular-passport and supporting documents.
Carry the issued authorization letter for airline check-in and Barbados Immigration.

policies.title: Haiti ordinary passport: qualifying permanent-resident or Green Card exception
policies.summary: A Haitian regular passport holder who is a permanent resident of the UK, United States, Canada, or Schengen countries, or holds a Green Card, does not require a Barbados visa under the Ministry’s stated exception.
conditions: This exception requires the stated qualifying residence or Green Card document; it is not unconditional Haitian ordinary-passport visa-free access.
The Ministry separately identifies diplomatic and official Haitian passports as visa-free; that special-document treatment is outside this ordinary-passport classification.
The visitor must still satisfy the published online form, passport, return-ticket, address, support, purpose, transit, and admission conditions.

policies.title: Indonesian nationals: outside foreign visitor visa scope
policies.summary: Indonesia's visitor-visa framework applies to foreigners, not Indonesian citizens.
conditions: This citizenship classification does not establish the document requirements for a particular Indonesian national, dual national, carrier, or border route.
It does not determine treatment when a dual Indonesian national presents another country's ordinary passport.

policies.title: Current BVK ordinary passports: Indonesia visa exemption
policies.summary: The listed ordinary passports are currently eligible for Indonesia's Bebas Visa Kunjungan (BVK) visitor-visa exemption.
conditions: BVK is a genuine visitor-visa exemption, not Visa on Arrival or e-VOA. The current official BVK list is applied alongside the current VOA list; where both facilities list a nationality, this policy uses the more favourable current BVK classification.
BVK authorizes a visitor stay of up to 30 days and is not extendable. Official BVK visitor purposes include tourism, family, and onward transit; it cannot be used for work or journalism.

A valid ordinary passport of at least six months and a return or onward ticket are required. Indonesian Immigration applies the facility at designated immigration checkpoints and retains admissibility discretion.
This policy does not establish work, residence, diplomatic, official, crew, calling-visa, refugee, alien travel-document, or other special-document treatment.

policies.title: Current VOA ordinary passports: Indonesia Visa on Arrival
policies.summary: The listed ordinary passports are eligible for Indonesia's Visa on Arrival (VOA) visitor route. e-VOA is an optional electronic application and payment channel for the same VOA category.
conditions: The current official list identifies these nationalities as VOA subjects. e-VOA does not change this normalized status to eVisa: Indonesia Immigration expressly describes e-VOA as electronic Visa on Arrival, while VOA remains obtainable and payable on arrival.

The B1 VOA permits one entry, an initial stay of up to 30 days, and one extension up to a total 60 days. It covers tourism, family visits, meetings/incentives/conventions/exhibitions, and onward transit, not work or residence.

e-VOA holders may use only the current specified airports and seaports. Ordinary VOA may instead be obtained at the applicable arrival immigration point; eligibility and facility availability are entry-point dependent.

The usual application materials include a passport valid at least six months and a return/onward ticket. A crew member joining a conveyance has a stated ticket exception. Entry and the stay permit remain subject to immigration assessment.
This policy does not cover calling-visa clearance, diplomatic, official, special, refugee, alien, or residence documents, or another visa purpose.

policies.title: Rwanda: universal ordinary-passport visa on arrival
policies.summary: DGI states that citizens of every country may receive a visa on arrival without applying before travel.
conditions: Applies to foreign ordinary-passport holders visiting Rwanda where nationality is the only modelled basis.

DGI states citizens of all countries may obtain a visa on arrival without prior application; its online and diplomatic pre-departure application routes are optional alternatives, not a nationality-wide eVisa requirement.
A genuine, acceptable travel document valid for at least six months, vaccination requirements, sufficient funds and final immigration-admissibility assessment remain required.
DGI describes fee-free arrival visas or passes for some regional, organisation-member and named-nationality cohorts; a fee waiver does not establish no-visa admission.
Does not decide citizenship, residence-based access, work, study, long-stay, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, special-document or case-specific entry rules.

policies.title: Rwanda: named ordinary passports with fee-waived 90-day arrival visas
policies.summary: DGI grants these named nationalities a 90-day visa free of charge upon arrival; the entry instrument remains a visa.
conditions: DGI names these nationalities for a 90-day visa free of charge upon arrival.
The source still describes a visa granted upon arrival. This is a fee-waived visa-on-arrival policy, not visa-free/no-visa admission.
The universal ordinary-passport visa-on-arrival conditions, admission checks and excluded purposes or documents continue to apply.

policies.title: First-list ordinary passports: 14-day Oman visa exemption
policies.summary: The named first-list nationalities may enter Oman without an entry visa for a short stay of up to 14 days, subject to the published visitor conditions.
conditions: The traveller must hold a passport valid for at least six months, a return ticket, confirmed hotel reservation, health insurance, and sufficient funds for the stay.
The stay is limited to 14 days and cannot be extended or converted to a residence visa.

CN is limited to the Ministry’s China entry, which expressly includes Hong Kong and Macau; HK and MO represent only those named special-administrative-region entries, not a PRC travel document or another special document.
The published accompanying spouse and children facility is not a passport-nationality-wide rule for an unaccompanied traveller, and is not modelled as separate passport access.

This policy does not establish work, residence, sponsored visit, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service, emergency, refugee, stateless, or other special-document treatment. Entry remains subject to border admission.

policies.title: Second-list ordinary passports: conditional 14-day Oman visa exemption
policies.summary: The named second-list nationalities may use Oman’s 14-day visa exemption only when the stated third-country-visa/residence or GCC-resident-profession condition is met.
conditions: The traveller must meet the same passport-validity, return-ticket, confirmed-hotel, health-insurance, and sufficient-funds conditions as the general 14-day exemption.

The national must either be a resident of, or hold a valid entry visa for, the United States, Canada, Australia, the United Kingdom, Japan, or a Schengen country; alternatively, the national may be a GCC resident in a qualifying resident-visa profession.
The stay is limited to 14 days and cannot be extended or transferred to a residence visa.
This is not unconditional visa-free access. It does not establish a nationality-wide eVisa, visa-on-arrival, employment, residence, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, or special-document route.

policies.title: GCC citizens: Oman visa-free entry
policies.summary: Citizens of the named Gulf Cooperation Council states do not require visas to enter Oman.
conditions: This policy follows the Foreign Ministry’s GCC-citizen rule and does not state a maximum visitor stay, an employment entitlement, or treatment of GCC residents who are not GCC citizens.
GCC residents of another nationality are instead subject to the separate conditional exemption’s qualifying-profession rule.
Diplomatic, official, service, special, emergency, travel-document, residence, work, purpose, and individual-admission requirements are not established by this ordinary-passport classification.

policies.title: Jamaican nationals: outside foreign visitor-visa scope
policies.summary: PICA's country table governs foreigners and Commonwealth nationals entering Jamaica, not Jamaican nationals.
conditions: This citizenship classification does not establish a particular traveller's document, carrier, dual-nationality, departure, residence, or admissibility treatment.
It must not be read as resolving entry when a dual Jamaican national presents another country's ordinary passport.

policies.title: PICA-listed ordinary passports: visa exemption for a short visit
policies.summary: PICA's live country table expressly marks these ordinary-nationality cohorts as not requiring a visa for entry to Jamaica; the stated duration and permitted short-visit purpose vary by row.
conditions: This is a nationality-specific ordinary short-visit exemption, not a finding that every PICA-listed document is visa-free. The exact table rows set differing stays and purposes: many state 30 or 90 days, the United States row states six months, and China and Macao are tourism-only examples.

PICA attaches health-document conditions to Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania and Slovenia, and attaches yellow-fever proof conditions to Bolivia, Paraguay and Peru. Those document conditions remain applicable and do not change the normalized visa-free status.

The specific Dominican Republic and Ireland rows also cover ordinary, diplomatic and official passports for stated tourism, business, cultural, transit, official, or diplomatic purposes. This policy only models the ordinary-passport short-visitor part of those rows.

A visa exemption neither authorizes work, residence, study, crew duties, nor overrides any purpose-specific requirement. It does not establish treatment of diplomatic, official, emergency, refugee, alien, certificate-of-identity, laissez-passer, military, seaman, or other non-ordinary documents.

MFAFT states that an immigration officer at the port of entry has final authority. Travellers must also use a valid, approved travel document; the embassy guidance adds passport validity for the visit and yellow-fever evidence when travelling from or through a WHO risk country.

policies.title: PICA-listed ordinary passports: visa at port of entry
policies.summary: PICA expressly says that these nationalities require a visa but may obtain it at the port of entry; this is normalized as visa on arrival, not visa-free or eVisa.
conditions: This route is limited to the PICA rows that literally state a visa may be obtained at the port of entry. It is not a general online-visa or prior-approval route.

Taiwan's row requires an Affidavit of Identity in addition to the port-of-entry visa. PICA's page separately says that holders of other accepted non-passport travel documents generally require a visa.

MFAFT says port-of-entry visa applicants must satisfy immigration authorities of their bona fides; its published checklist includes a valid passport, onward or return ticket and sufficient funds/accommodation. Admission remains for the immigration officer to decide.
The policy does not establish diplomatic, official, refugee, alien-document, residence, work, study, crew, transit, or any unlisted-special-document treatment.

policies.title: PICA-listed ordinary passports: visa required before travel
policies.summary: PICA's current country table requires a visa for these ordinary-passport cohorts and does not give them the port-of-entry visa route; the MFAFT-hosted Immigration Unit listing expressly supplies Timor-Leste as PTA.
conditions: For Albania, Belarus, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Bulgaria, Croatia, Honduras, Kazakhstan, Moldova, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Romania and Serbia, PICA's country-specific text gives a narrow visa waiver for a tourist stay of 30 days or less only when the traveller holds the named valid United States, Canadian, United Kingdom or Schengen visa, with listed vaccination evidence where required. That is a third-country-document condition, not passport-wide visa-free access or a Jamaican visa on arrival.

Kosovo's PICA row requires both a visa and an Affidavit of Identity. Haiti and Cuba retain the table's diplomatic/official passport exceptions, which do not alter their ordinary-passport prior-visa classification.

The current PICA row for the United Arab Emirates says visa required. A 2019 MFAFT announcement described an interim UAE port-of-entry arrangement pending an online system; the later live PICA table is used as the current operational rule, and this historical discrepancy is retained in the related snapshot conflict.

MFAFT instructs a person whose passport nationality requires a visa to apply at the Jamaican consular post where they live or the nearest one. Visa possession does not guarantee admission; purpose, work, residence, transit, document and immigration-admissibility rules remain separate.

MFAFT separately says a person visiting as part of a cruise does not need a visa, while an unrecognised-country national needs an Affidavit of Identity. This travel-mode or document exception is not a passport-wide ordinary visitor status and does not change this cohort.

No generic eVisa or ETA is inferred from the availability of consular processing. This policy does not establish treatment of special, diplomatic, official, refugee, alien, emergency, travel-document, crew, or resident classes.

application.label: Jamaica MFAFT visa guidance
steps: Confirm the nationality and document rule in PICA's country table.
Apply to the Jamaican consular post in the country of residence or nearest Jamaican consular post.
Do not travel on the assumption that a visa guarantees admission; present all applicable entry documents to immigration.

policies.title: Zambia: listed ordinary passports that do not require a visa
policies.summary: DGI expressly places these nationalities in its no-visa entry category.
conditions: Ordinary-passport nationality classification only. DGI's country list says these nationals do not require a visa to enter Zambia.

For air arrival, non-citizens/non-residents need a valid return air ticket; for land or water arrival, they need funds for their stay and departure. Admission remains subject to immigration examination.
This does not establish access for diplomatic, official, service, emergency, refugee, stateless or other special travel documents, residents, workers, students, crew, or case-specific travel.
Transit, including direct airside transit, and purpose-specific requirements are separate rules.

policies.title: Zambia: Zambian citizenship entry
policies.summary: Current Department of Immigration arrival guidance confines the visa requirement to qualifying non-citizens or non-residents; the same-country ordinary-passport relationship is normalized as citizenship, not a foreign visitor visa-free route.
conditions: DGI's arrival guidance distinguishes Zambian citizens from visa-requiring non-citizens; the no-visa schedule also expressly includes Zambia. This does not decide passport/document, dual-nationality, border, security or individual-admissibility formalities.
Direct-air-transit, resident, work, study, diplomatic, official, service and special-document rules are outside this nationality baseline.

policies.title: Zambia: listed ordinary passports eligible for visa on arrival
policies.summary: DGI expressly allows these nationalities to get a visa at any Zambian port of entry.
conditions: DGI states these nationalities may receive a visa on arrival at any port of entry or from selected Zambian missions.
The same page says they may apply online, but that optional online route does not replace the expressly available arrival-visa route or make this a nationality-wide eVisa classification.

For arrival issuance, DGI requires host information and a physical Zambia address, a passport valid at least six months from entry with at least three full blank pages, and either a return air ticket or sufficient funds for land/water arrival.
Purpose, residence, employment, study, crew, transit, diplomatic, official, special-document and individual admissibility rules remain separate.

policies.title: Zambia: listed ordinary passports requiring prior-clearance eVisa
policies.summary: DGI requires these nationalities to apply online and receive an approval letter before travelling to Zambia.
conditions: DGI says this category requires advance clearance, online application through eServices, and an approval letter before travel; it cannot use a visa-on-arrival route.
The electronic approval is an eVisa for the model's pre-travel-entry category; it does not guarantee admission, which remains subject to immigration examination.
Bring the approval letter and receipt to entry. DGI states eVisa approval-letter holders may enter through any port of entry.
DGI notes that applicants under 16 cannot make an eVisa application themselves and must be included in an adult's application when travelling with an adult.
Does not decide special documents, diplomatic/official treatment, residence, employment, study, crew, transit or case-specific purpose rules.

application.label: Zambia Department of Immigration eServices visa application
steps: Create or use an eServices account and select the visa application.
Complete Form 16, upload the required documents, review the application and pay online.
Receive and print the approval letter before travel; present the letter and receipt to the Immigration Officer.

policies.title: Ecuadorian nationals: outside foreign visitor-visa scope
policies.summary: The Human Mobility Regulation's tourist-entry rules govern foreign persons, not Ecuadorian nationals presenting an Ecuadorian passport.
conditions: This classification does not establish entry treatment for dual nationals presenting another passport, residence, migration-registration, departure, document-validity, or individual-admissibility requirements.

policies.title: Named ordinary passports: transitory visitor eVisa required before travel
policies.summary: Effective 1 September 2025, Ecuador's foreign ministry expressly requires the named nationalities to obtain the electronically issued Visa de Visitante Temporal de Transeúnte before entering Ecuador.
conditions: The announcement calls this authorization a Visa de Visitante Temporal de Transeúnte under the 2025 reform to Article 66 of the Organic Law on Human Mobility. It must be requested while the applicant is outside Ecuador through the ministry's official digital service.

The Foreign Ministry describes the eVISAS service as electronic visas processed 100% online. Its current guide says the approved electronic visa is sent by email for the traveller to download and present, so this is normalized as eVisa rather than a non-electronic advance visa, ETA, or visa on arrival.

The foreign ministry's visitor regulation separately provides that a tourist may not perform work or economic activity. Passport validity, visa validity, purpose, route, residence, transit, diplomatic or official document, security, prior immigration history, and border-admission requirements remain separate and are not established by this nationality rule.

application.label: Ecuador Foreign Ministry digital visa service
steps: Apply for the transitory temporary visitor visa from outside Ecuador through the ministry's digital service.
Provide the documents and pay the amounts required for the individual application.
Download the eVisa delivered by email and present it with all required documents to migration control; issuance does not itself establish admission.

policies.title: Named South American ordinary passports: visitor entry up to 180 days
policies.summary: The current exhaustive required-visa list does not include these named South American nationalities, and the Human Mobility Regulation allows South American tourists up to 180 days in a year.
conditions: The 180-day figure is the maximum that migration control may grant to a South American tourist in one year; it is not a guaranteed stay or an authorization for employment or economic activity.

The classification rests on the Foreign Ministry's explicit current list of all nationalities for which Ecuador requires a visa, read with the visitor-stay rule. It does not establish national-identity-card use, residence, work, transit, diplomatic, official, emergency, refugee, or other special-document treatment.

Entry remains subject to presenting an identity-verifying travel document, migration-control verification of the invoked status, security and admissibility requirements, and any current health or carrier requirements.

policies.title: Other expressly unlisted ordinary foreign passports: visitor exemption up to 90 days
policies.summary: Ecuador's foreign ministry expressly identifies the complete current nationality list for which a visa is required; the other named foreign ordinary-passport codes are therefore visitor-exempt for the regulation's normal maximum of 90 days in one year.
conditions: This complement is inferred only from the ministry's explicit current statement that the listed countries are those whose nationals are required to hold a visa. The current source does not state a nationality-wide eVisa, ETA, arrival-visa, or electronic travel-authorization route for this complement.

A foreign tourist may remain for a maximum of 90 days from the first entry in a year and may apply once for an extension of up to 90 further days under the regulation. This normal 90-day rule does not replace the distinct South American maximum.

The traveller must present a travel document verifying identity and satisfy the migration-control officer that the claimed immigration status applies. No work or economic activity is authorized by tourist entry.

This is limited to ordinary foreign passports. It does not establish diplomatic, official, service, emergency, refugee, stateless, laissez-passer, residence, employment, transit, special-purpose, or individual security/admissibility treatment.

policies.title: Argentine nationals: outside foreign visitor-visa scope
policies.summary: DNM's tourist visa matrix applies to foreign passport nationalities, not Argentine nationals.
conditions: This classification does not establish the documents, carrier requirements, dual-national treatment, exit conditions, or admission decision for a particular Argentine national.
It does not resolve entry when a dual national presents a different country's ordinary passport.

policies.title: DNM-listed ordinary passports: tourist visa exemption
policies.summary: DNM's exhaustive ordinary-tourist passport matrix has no visa requirement in the ordinary-passport column for these nationalities.
conditions: This is limited to the DNM matrix's ordinary-passport tourist column. Blank ordinary-tourist cells are treated as the table's express visa-exempt entry rule; no complement is inferred.

A tourist enters for rest or recreation, is normally authorized for up to three months, may request one comparable extension, and may not perform remunerated work. Transit, frontier transit, crew, academic, medical, special, work, study, and residence are separate Migration Law categories.

Mercosur and associated-national rows remain ordinary visa-exempt entries, but DNM separately permits Brazil, Bolivia, Uruguay, Paraguay, Chile, Peru, Venezuela, Ecuador and Colombia to use specified valid national identity or travel documents. This passport policy does not extend that document option to other nationalities.

The ordinary-passport table separately shows diplomatic/service outcomes for some nationalities. This policy does not establish diplomatic, official, service, refugee, alien, emergency, laissez-passer, certificate-of-travel, residence, or other special-document treatment. Admission and any separate health, carrier, or border control requirements remain applicable.

policies.title: China, Dominican Republic and India: conditional ordinary tourist visa exemption
policies.summary: Current 2025 Argentine resolutions waive both a consular visa and AVE for these ordinary passports only when the traveller presents the specified valid United States visa and stays within the stated tourist/business scope.
conditions: China and Dominican Republic require an ordinary passport plus a valid, current United States visa of a similar migratory category. Dominican Republic is tourist-only, up to 90 days; China is tourist or the specified business category, up to 30 days.

India requires an ordinary passport plus a valid, current United States visa of a similar migratory category, verified as required; it is tourist-only and up to 90 days. Its rule took effect 28 August 2025.

These are conditional exemptions, not general visa-free status for the passport codes. A person outside the stated conditions must obtain a consular visa; no change of migratory category is allowed and a single comparable extension remains subject to DNM assessment.

DNM's AVE portal also mentions a United States green card for China, while Resolution 316/2025's operative text specifies a valid United States visa. The resolution is treated as controlling for this legal condition; the portal wording is preserved as an operational discrepancy for review.

policies.title: DNM-listed ordinary passports: AVE electronic travel authorization
policies.summary: The listed ordinary passport nationalities are eligible to seek Argentina's AVE electronic travel authorization instead of a consular tourist visa only when they meet DNM's additional United States document and history requirements.
conditions: AVE is an electronic travel authorization, not an eVisa or visa-on-arrival. It applies to valid ordinary passports travelling as tourists, only for nationalities in DNM's current AVE list.

An applicant must hold a valid United States B2, J, B1, O, P, E or H-1B visa covering the AVE processing, AVE validity and intended Argentine stay. A person from a United States visa-exempt jurisdiction may instead show a verified U.S. entry in the preceding two years, a valid ESTA, or one of the stated visas.

DNM says an AVE tourist authorization is valid for three months, permits a three-month tourist stay from first entry with multiple entries/exits, and may be extended once after DNM assessment. DNM has up to 20 working days to decide and may extend that period.

Taiwan's ordinary-tourist matrix row states 'visa / travel certificate'; AVE eligibility does not erase document-recognition or certificate requirements. The same caution applies to every diplomatic, official, service, special, refugee, alien, residence, work, study, crew, transit, or other non-ordinary-document case.
Approval is not guaranteed. Complete the fee step and online application through DNM; do not enter before the authorization is issued.

application.label: Argentina DNM AVE Global
application.processingTime: DNM states up to 20 working days for tourist AVE decisions, extendable when necessary.
steps: Confirm that the passport nationality is on DNM's current AVE list and that the additional United States eligibility evidence is valid.
Use DNM's AVE portal to pay the fee and submit the online application.
Wait for DNM's decision before travelling; an AVE is not an arrival-issued visa.

policies.title: DNM-listed ordinary passports: consular tourist visa required
policies.summary: DNM's exhaustive ordinary-tourist matrix expressly marks these nationalities 'REQUIERE VISA' or a visa/travel-certificate requirement. Any separate AVE or 2025 conditional United States-visa exception is retained as a narrow overlapping route, not silently converted into general visa-free access.
conditions: This policy consists only of DNM's explicit ordinary-tourist rows marked 'REQUIERE VISA' (and Kosovo/Taiwan's 'visa / travel certificate' rows). It is not a nationality complement inferred outside the official matrix.

China, India and the Dominican Republic have the separate conditional United States-visa tourist exemptions in the other policy; all three still display as visa-required in the matrix for travellers without that exception. The AVE-eligible countries likewise remain visa-required if the AVE conditions or authorization are absent.

For the consular tourist visa route, Argentina's official service guidance requires a passport valid for at least six months, a completed application, financial proof, return reservation, accommodation/itinerary or invitation, fee and consular interview. Apply through the Argentine consular representation with jurisdiction.

The tourist category is for rest/recreation, normally up to three months and renewable once; it does not permit remunerated work. Transit, crew, work, study, residence, diplomatic/official/service, refugee, special travel certificate and other Migration Law categories are separate and cannot be inferred from this ordinary-passport policy.

application.label: Argentina tourist visa guidance
steps: Confirm the ordinary-passport rule and whether a separate AVE or statutory conditional exemption applies.
Contact the competent Argentine consular representation to arrange the required tourist-visa interview.
Submit the official travel, financial, passport, itinerary/accommodation and other consular documents before travel.

policies.title: Nepal: Indian ordinary passports with no visa required
policies.summary: TIA Immigration expressly says Indian citizens do not need a visa to enter Nepal.
conditions: Ordinary-passport nationality result only. TIA Immigration says Indian citizens may enter using a valid passport without a visa.
The source also describes voter-card and minor-document alternatives for Indian citizens without a passport; those document-specific routes are outside this ordinary-passport policy.
Does not decide residence, work, study, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service, special-document, or case-specific entry rules.

policies.title: Nepal: ordinary passports eligible for tourist visa on arrival
policies.summary: Nepal's current tourist-visa guidance and TIA's exhaustive exception list support visa on arrival for all listed foreign ordinary passports except India and the twelve prior-visa nationalities.
conditions: For ordinary short-visit/tourist treatment, TIA facilitates visa on arrival; the listed twelve nationalities in the separate prior-visa policy are expressly ineligible for arrival issuance, and Indian citizens are visa-free.

DoI's online tourist form may be completed before arrival or at airport kiosks, then the traveller pays at the counter and the immigration officer issues the visa. This is arrival processing, not a nationality-wide eVisa classification.
Tourist visa-on-arrival options are 15, 30 or 90 days; tourist stay, including extensions, is subject to Nepal's stated visa-year limits and immigration determination.

SAARC nationals Bangladesh, Bhutan, Maldives, Pakistan and Sri Lanka receive a gratis visa for up to 30 days on their first visit in a visa year; this is a fee-free visa on arrival, not no-visa admission. Afghanistan remains a named arrival-visa exclusion.

China, child, NRN-card, diplomatic, official, service, residence, work, study, transit, crew, special-document and case-specific rules are not flattened into this ordinary-passport nationality result.

policies.title: Nepal: SAARC ordinary passports with fee-free tourist visa on arrival
policies.summary: Nepal grants these non-Indian, non-Afghan SAARC citizens a gratis visa for up to 30 days on the first visit of a visa year.
conditions: This is a fee-free tourist visa, not no-visa entry, and is limited to up to 30 days on the first visit in a given visa year.
Afghanistan is a SAARC member but is expressly ineligible for visa on arrival and is therefore excluded from this group; Indian citizens are separately visa-free.
All ordinary-passport arrival conditions and exclusions of the overlapping universal visa-on-arrival policy continue to apply.

policies.title: Nepal: ordinary passports not eligible for visa on arrival
policies.summary: TIA Immigration expressly excludes these nationalities from visa on arrival; obtain an appropriate visitor visa before travel.
conditions: TIA Immigration expressly names these nationalities as not eligible for visa on arrival. They require an appropriate visa arranged before travel through Nepal's pre-departure visa channels.

This policy does not call an online form eVisa: DoI's ordinary tourist online form is also used for counter-issued visa-on-arrival processing, and the reviewed sources do not establish an exclusive nationality-wide electronic issuance route for this group.
Does not decide diplomatic, official, service, special-document, refugee, residence, work, study, crew, transit or case-specific treatment.

policies.title: Maldives: foreign ordinary passports with tourist visa on arrival
policies.summary: Maldives Immigration grants the tourist visa on arrival to foreign tourists without visa pre-approval, subject to the separate Israeli-passport prohibition.
conditions: Applies only to foreign ordinary passports for tourism/short visitor travel. Maldives Immigration says tourist visas are granted on arrival and tourists do not require visa pre-approval.
A Traveller Declaration is mandatory within 96 hours before the arriving flight and is a free self-declaration. It is not an ETA or eVisa and does not replace arrival issuance.

Arrival requires an MRZ passport or travel document with at least one month validity (no extended-validity passports), a complete itinerary with confirmed return journey, prepaid registered accommodation and sufficient funds, or a pre-approved Maldives Immigration sponsorship visa; onward-entry requirements and applicable yellow-fever certification also apply.
Immigration officers determine admissibility at the port of entry. The reviewed current tourist-visa page does not state a fixed initial tourist-visa duration, so this candidate does not infer one.

Does not classify residence, work, business, meeting/conference, dependent, marriage, transit without clearing arrival immigration, crew, diplomatic, official, service, refugee, stateless, emergency or other special-document cases.

policies.title: Maldives: citizenship treatment
policies.summary: The destination's own ordinary-passport code is represented as citizenship rather than a foreign-entry visa result.
conditions: This represents a Maldivian citizen holding an ordinary Maldivian passport, not foreign visitor admission.
Does not classify dual-nationality, foreign residence, diplomatic, official, emergency or other document-specific circumstances.

policies.title: Seychellois nationals: outside foreign visitor-entry scope
policies.summary: The visitor permit and foreign-visitor Travel Authorisation framework does not establish entry requirements for Seychellois nationals travelling on a Seychelles passport.
conditions: This classification does not establish the departure-form, carrier, document, dual-nationality, permit-holder, or admission treatment of a particular Seychellois national.
The Electronic Border System separately describes an Embarkation Information Form for Seychellois citizens and permit holders leaving Seychelles; it is not a visitor ETA classification.

policies.title: All foreign ordinary passports: no visa, mandatory pre-travel ETA and visitor permit on arrival
policies.summary: Seychelles does not require an entry visa regardless of nationality and issues the Visitor's Permit on arrival, but every foreign ordinary visitor must first obtain a Travel Authorisation/ETA before departure. The mandatory pre-travel authorization is normalized as eta.
conditions: Seychelles' Immigration guidance expressly distinguishes a no-visa system from the mandatory pre-departure Electronic Travel Authorisation. For this repository's access taxonomy, the live mandatory ETA is the operative entry status and supersedes an otherwise visa_free label; it does not turn the Visitor's Permit into a visa on arrival or an eVisa.

The Visitor's Permit is issued on arrival, initially for up to three months and free for that first period. It may be extended in successive periods of up to three months to a maximum of twelve months if the visitor continues to meet the conditions; each extension costs SCR 5,000.

A visitor must not be a prohibited immigrant or already hold a permit entitling residence; must have a valid return/onward ticket, confirmed accommodation and sufficient funds. Immigration's general entry guidance states a minimum of US$150 or equivalent per day.

The visitor route covers holiday, pleasure, business, and visits to friends/family. It does not permit paid or unpaid full-time or part-time work by a non-Seychellois; a Gainful Occupation Permit is separate. Residence, student, dependant, international-trade-zone, crew, maritime, diplomatic, transit, refugee, alien-document, laissez-passer, and other special-document cases are not established by this ordinary visitor policy.

A valid passport or other Seychelles-recognised travel document is required and must remain valid through the intended stay and return to the country of origin/residence.
