policies.title: Bahrain: GCC citizens do not need an entry visa
policies.summary: The Bahrain National Portal expressly exempts citizens of Kuwait, Oman, the United Arab Emirates, Saudi Arabia and Qatar from Bahrain’s entry-visa requirement.
conditions: Applies to citizenship of the five named GCC states, not merely residence in a GCC state.
The National Portal says other nationalities require an entry visa; this is not a visa-on-arrival, ETA, or eVisa.
NPRA separately offers electronic visas to GCC residents who meet its status and document conditions; that route does not alter the named GCC citizen exemption.
Same-flight or same-airport transit is separately visa-free under the Bahrain AIP and is outside this ordinary visitor classification.
Does not classify work, residence, family sponsorship, transit requiring entry, crew, diplomatic, official, service, UN, emergency, refugee, or other special-document entry.

policies.title: Bahrain: citizenship treatment
policies.summary: A Bahraini ordinary passport belongs to a Bahraini citizen and is not a foreign visitor-visa case.
conditions: Applies to Bahraini citizens holding a Bahraini ordinary passport.
Does not decide foreign residence, dual-national document choice, or foreign visitor treatment.

policies.title: Qatari nationals: outside foreign visitor scope
policies.summary: The foreign visitor visa framework does not establish entry treatment for Qatari passport holders.
conditions: This does not determine dual-national, resident, departure, identity-document or individual admission treatment.

policies.title: GCC citizens: no visa required
policies.summary: Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman, Saudi Arabia and UAE nationals may visit Qatar without a visa on the current Hayya/Qatar Tourism guidance.
conditions: The guidance says GCC nationals need a passport or GCC ID. This policy is nationality-based and does not establish the separate GCC-resident or accompanying-person Hayya routes for other passports.

policies.title: Named ordinary passports: arrival-issued visitor waiver or visa
policies.summary: The current Qatar Tourism passport wizard places these nationalities in arrival-entry paths. Although Qatar Tourism now calls the former free visa-on-arrival route “visa-free”, MOI describes on-arrival visas and passport stickers; this operational category is normalized as visa_on_arrival.
conditions: Passport-level routes vary: some are free arrival waivers, while IR, MU, ME, TW, PK, TH and UA are displayed with paid and/or Discover Qatar hotel-reservation arrival routes. Hayya A1/A2/A3 may be an advance alternative where the wizard says so; optional online processing does not replace an available arrival status.

Current MOI guidance requires a passport valid at least three months, onward/return ticket and compulsory health insurance for on-arrival visitors; particular routes also require a hotel booking, Discover Qatar booking, cash/card or fees. Check the live selector for the exact passport route and duration.

The older MOI 90-day schedule publishes six-month passport validity, onward ticket and a passport sticker; its duration lists do not exactly match the current Qatar Tourism selector. Treat the individual live selector and border decision as controlling.

A residence in GCC, or residence/valid visa in Schengen, UK, US, Australia, New Zealand or Canada, can create distinct document-conditioned A2/A3 routes. It is not a nationality-wide rule. Transit, Qatar-Oman joint visas, employment, residence, diplomatic/official, temporary travel documents and special cases are separate.

policies.title: Other passport codes listed by the visa wizard: advance Hayya eVisa
policies.summary: For these ordinary-passport codes, the current Qatar Tourism selector directs an A1 Entry Visa through Hayya rather than an arrival route. It is normalized as evisa.
conditions: Apply for the A1 Entry Visa through Hayya before travel; the selector states that a hotel reservation is required during application and visa fee is payable after approval.

The eVisa route is for tourism and remains subject to passport, accommodation, insurance, funds, health, security and admission requirements. It does not create work, residence, transit, diplomatic/official or special-document rights.

application.label: Hayya Tourist E-Visas
steps: Select the appropriate A1 visitor route in Hayya before travel.
Provide the required hotel reservation and other requested travel documentation, then complete payment after approval as instructed.
Carry the approved electronic visa and supporting documents; admission remains subject to Qatar border control.

policies.title: Saudi nationals: outside foreign visitor scope
policies.summary: Saudi citizens do not receive a foreign visitor-entry classification when travelling on an ordinary Saudi passport.
conditions: This does not determine a dual national’s treatment when presenting another passport, nor any case-specific exit, security or border requirement.

policies.title: Current nationality-wide ordinary-passport visa-on-arrival cohort
policies.summary: The live Saudi Tourism Authority visa-regulations widget places these passport nationalities in groups that offer both eVisa and visa on arrival. Under the easiest-access taxonomy, the direct arrival route is visa_on_arrival.
conditions: The live widget offers either an eVisa or a visa on arrival. For arrival issuance, it directs the traveller to a self-service KIOSK or passport-control office at the Saudi entry point.

The widget states that both eVisa and visa on arrival may be single- or multiple-entry. Multiple entry is valid for one year and allows no more than 90 consecutive days; single entry is valid for three months and allows no more than 90 consecutive days.

Visitors must have a passport valid at least six months beyond entry, except that US citizens may enter while the passport remains valid. Travellers under 18 may need to travel with a parent, grandparent, or adult sibling.

Tourism and Umrah are within the visitor materials; work, study, residence, Hajj, transit, crew, diplomatic, special-document and other purpose routes are outside this ordinary-passport visitor classification. Umrah permits may be required through Nusuk.
Approval or arrival issuance does not guarantee admission; border, security, document and local-law requirements remain applicable.

The older eVisa terms and portal lists are not fully concordant with the live widget. The live route API is used for route precedence; Brazil remains unresolved because it appears on an older public list but is noneligible in the current widget.

policies.title: Russian ordinary passport: visa-free short visitor entry
policies.summary: The live Saudi Tourism Authority visa-regulations widget explicitly says Russian passport holders need no visa or prior application, confirming that the December 2025 agreement is operational.
conditions: The widget says a valid Russian passport permits entry on arrival without a visa or prior application, with no visa, exemption or medical-insurance fee.
The limit is up to 90 days in a calendar year, in one continuous stay or across visits, for tourism, leisure, business visits and Umrah.

Work, study, residence, Hajj, transit, crew, special-document and case-specific entry treatment are outside this ordinary-passport short-visitor classification. Umrah permits may be required through Nusuk.

The older eVisa terms still list Russia as eVisa-eligible; the current live country group and route content expressly identify visa exemption and are preferred. Admission remains subject to border and security requirements.

policies.title: GCC nationals: visa-free entry
policies.summary: The live Saudi Tourism Authority visa-regulations widget says GCC nationals do not need a visa and may travel using an ID or passport.
conditions: This policy covers ordinary passport holders from the five other GCC member states; the Saudi citizen pair is classified separately as citizenship.

The widget permits travel using an ID or passport. This record concerns ordinary passports and does not resolve residence, work, study, Hajj, transit, crew, special-document or case-specific treatment.
Admission remains subject to border, security, document and local-law requirements.

policies.title: Group D nationalities: advance embassy or consulate visa
policies.summary: The live Saudi Tourism Authority visa-regulations widget places these nationalities in Group D and presents only the Embassy/Consulate/Tasheer visitor-visa route, not an eVisa or visa-on-arrival route.
conditions: The widget requires an embassy, consulate, or Tasheer visa application, including the stated residence proof, return ticket, employment proof, financial-solvency evidence, flight itinerary, identification and Saudi residence address.
Entry count, duration and approval are determined by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs; the widget describes a multiple-entry visitor visa as valid for one year and stays up to 90 days.

This record does not establish eVisa, visa-on-arrival, transit, work, study, residence, Hajj, crew, diplomatic, special-document or case-specific treatment. Border and security checks remain applicable.

policies.title: Jordanian citizenship is outside the foreign visitor-visa schedule
policies.summary: Jordan's restricted and non-restricted foreign-nationality schedule does not establish visitor-visa treatment for a Jordanian passport holder.
conditions: This classification does not determine a dual national's document obligations, Jordanian passport validity, departure restrictions, military-service matters or case-specific border treatment.

policies.title: Jordan nationalities requiring prior visa approval
policies.summary: The Ministry of Interior expressly classifies these 53 nationalities as restricted and requiring prior approval before travel to Jordan.
conditions: The Ministry expressly treats this group as requiring prior approval. Its E-services manual distinguishes their other visa applications from the electronic-visa route for nationalities that do not require prior approval; this is therefore visa_required, not evisa.
The Ministry's schedule is split into 14 Asian, 37 African and two South American nationalities. Its spellings are normalized to the catalog codes without expanding the list.
All travel-pass documents issued by any country are treated as restricted except a travel pass issued by Vatican City; that document rule is not generalized to ordinary Vatican passports.

An application must be submitted from outside Jordan. The Ministry may require an in-person interview at a Jordanian embassy, and its portal supports electronic submission, status inquiry and payment.

This policy does not establish duration, entries, extension, fee, sponsor or guarantee requirements, work, study, transit, residence, diplomatic, official, service, emergency, refugee, stateless or other special-document treatment.

Approval does not itself guarantee admission. Passport validity, purpose, accommodation, funds, onward travel, health, public-order, security and individual admissibility requirements remain applicable.

application.label: Jordan Ministry of Interior Visit Visa E-Service
steps: Register an account with an email address on the Ministry of Interior electronic-services portal.
Select the Visit Visa service and submit the application while outside Jordan.
Track the application through the account and pay the applicable service charge or other requested amount.
Attend a Jordanian embassy interview if the Ministry requests one and retain the electronic application number.

policies.title: United Arab Emirates citizenship
policies.summary: A UAE ordinary passport belongs to a UAE citizen and is outside the foreign visitor-visa schedule.
conditions: Does not decide a dual national’s document choice, residence, departure, work, military-service, or case-specific border treatment.

policies.title: GCC citizens: visa-free entry
policies.summary: UAE Government guidance expressly says GCC citizens do not need a visa to enter the UAE.
conditions: The traveller must produce a GCC-country passport or national ID card at entry. This is a citizen rule, not a GCC-resident rule.
The separate GCC-resident electronic visa applies to qualifying residents and companions and does not alter this GCC-citizen exemption.
The reviewed sources do not establish work, residence, transit requiring entry, diplomatic, official, service, emergency, refugee, or other special-document treatment.

policies.title: MOFA schedule: named visa-free ordinary passport entries
policies.summary: The current MOFA non-citizen schedule marks these named nationality entries Visa Free.
conditions: This maps the schedule country/passport entries only. It does not establish a common duration, entry count, extension, employment right, residence right, or special-document rule.
UAE Government guidance says passports must be valid for at least six months from entry and that arrival eligibility may change; admission remains subject to border and security decisions.

Hong Kong is limited to the schedule named Hong Kong SAR entry; it does not establish PRC, Macao, Taiwan, travel-document, British National (Overseas), or another special passport treatment. Kosovo and Vatican likewise represent only their named ordinary-country entries.
Do not re-label an optional sponsor, airline, hotel, agency, residence-conditioned, transit, or other purpose-specific route as the nationality-wide default.

policies.title: MOFA named ordinary passports: advance electronic tourist visa
policies.summary: MOFA marks these nationalities Visa Required rather than Visa Free. The UAE’s all-nationalities self-sponsored five-year tourist visa is applied for and issued electronically, so the nationality-wide least-onerous advance route is normalized as evisa.
conditions: MOFA's Visa Required label establishes that no visa-free nationality default applies. UAE Government guidance makes a self-sponsored five-year tourist visa available to all nationalities, and ICP states that the visa is received by email and downloadable electronically; this supports evisa, not visa_on_arrival or traditional visa_required, under the project taxonomy.

The five-year route has material eligibility conditions, including the stated funds, UAE-valid health insurance and onward/return ticket. Approval and border admission remain discretionary; it does not establish a no-document or no-fee route.

The ICP 25 June 2026 announcement creates a separate residence-conditioned 14- or 60-day entry-visa option for India, Indonesia, Viet Nam, Thailand, the Philippines, Kenya, and South Africa. It does not replace the nationality-wide electronic tourist-visa route.

For that conditional route, the qualifying residence permit must be from the US, an EU Member State, UK, Singapore, Japan, South Korea, Australia, New Zealand or Canada; accompanying family members must meet the stated nationality and relationship conditions.
No conclusion is drawn about residence, work, study, transit, diplomatic, official, service, emergency, refugee, stateless, travel-document, or other special-document routes.

application.label: ICP Issuance of a Visa
steps: Select the suitable tourism/visit visa category on ICP Smart Services or the ICP Smart App.
Submit the application, required passport and supporting documents, and pay the applicable fees.
After approval, download the electronically issued visa received by email and carry the required supporting documents for border inspection.

policies.title: Kuwaiti nationals: outside foreign visitor scope
policies.summary: A Kuwaiti ordinary passport belongs to a Kuwaiti citizen and is not a foreign visitor-visa case.
conditions: This does not decide dual-national document choice, foreign residence, exit, security, or individual admission treatment.

policies.title: GCC citizens: visa-free entry using national identification
policies.summary: Kuwait's 2024 residency-law report says GCC citizens may enter and leave Kuwait using their national identity cards under Ministry of Interior regulations and inter-state agreements; this is normalized as visa_free rather than a resident or sponsor visa.
conditions: This is a GCC-citizenship right for Bahraini, Omani, Qatari, Saudi and UAE nationals. It is not an eVisa or visa-on-arrival route and does not extend to a non-GCC passport holder merely resident in a GCC state.

The cited report makes the national-ID entry right subject to Ministry of Interior regulations and agreements with the relevant GCC states; identity, border, security and individual-admission requirements remain applicable.
This ordinary-passport classification does not establish work, study, residence, family, companion, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, emergency-document or other special-case treatment.

policies.title: Named ordinary passports: visa on arrival
policies.summary: The current Ministry of Interior Kuwait Visa endpoint explicitly marks these 53 nationality records as visaOnArrival.
conditions: The current endpoint establishes visa-on-arrival eligibility for these nationalities but does not itself state a complete purpose, document, duration, passport-type or port-condition schedule. This record does not manufacture conditions absent from that source.

The Ministry of Interior online-visa terms separately require online applicants to use the official site, normally have a passport valid for six months, provide specified travel documents, and observe a maximum 90-day stay unless the issued visa says otherwise. Those online-application conditions are not treated as a replacement for the available arrival route.

Any eVisa alternative, and any entry route based on residence, profession, sponsor, family, employment, study, transit, diplomatic or special-document facts, is separate from this nationality-wide ordinary-passport arrival classification.
Issuance or entry remains subject to Ministry of Interior security review and border discretion.

policies.title: Lebanese citizenship
policies.summary: A Lebanese ordinary passport belongs to a Lebanese citizen and is outside the foreign visitor-visa schedule.
conditions: Does not decide a dual national document choice, residence, departure, work, military service, or case-specific border treatment.

policies.title: GCC and Jordanian ordinary passports: tourist visa at border
policies.summary: General Security says a free three-month Jordanian or six-month GCC visa is stamped at passport or other border posts for tourism.
conditions: The source simultaneously calls GCC and Jordanian tourists exempt from entry visas but expressly says the three- or six-month visa is stamped and granted at border posts. This is normalized as visa_on_arrival, not visa_free.
Jordanian travellers need a passport with a national number. The stated periods can be extended up to one year by General Security.

Companion, domestic-worker, driver, bodyguard, family, professional, residence, national-ID, and land-driver provisions are conditional and do not establish an ordinary foreign-passport exemption outside the named cohort.

policies.title: Named ordinary passports: automatic one-month tourist visa
policies.summary: General Security named tourism schedule grants these ordinary-passport nationalities a free one-month visa, extendable to three months; Turkey has a separately stated airport/border tourist visa.
conditions: The core named schedule grants a cost-free one-month tourist visa, extendable to three months; General Security distinguishes immediate from anticipated and consular issuance. Turkey is expressly a free multiple-entry three-month visa at airport and border posts.

Passport/document exceptions are not ordinary-passport rules: emergency passports, Ukraine child travel documents, Poland temporary passports, travel passes, Palestinian passports, refugee/alien documents, diplomatic/official/service passports, domestic workers, artists, and women in specified professions have separate conditions or prior approval.

Purpose, address notification, passport validity, funds, ticket, accommodation, age/sex, profession, residence, prior visit, security, work, study, transit, extension, and admissibility conditions remain applicable.

Iraq is retained as unresolved: Article Two gives a broad automatic tourist rule, while the later Article Eight describes automatic Iraqi visas only for named trader, doctor and engineer categories. The current page does not reconcile those scopes.

policies.title: Article Eight: named ordinary passports receive tourist visa at border
policies.summary: Article Eight expressly grants a one-month visa, extendable to three months, to the named tourists at entry when its ticket, accommodation/contact and funds conditions are met. It is normalized as visa_on_arrival.
conditions: A round-trip airline ticket, hotel reservation or residential address and telephone number, and USD 2,000 (or an equivalent certified bank cheque) are required. Holders of a visa granted abroad by Lebanese missions or General Security are exempt from those stated documents.
Jordan is also named in Article Eight but remains in the separate GCC/Jordan policy, which already establishes its border-visa route.

Egypt and Ghana are excluded from this nationality-only policy because Article Ten imposes prior General Security authorization for female tourists from those countries; the page does not state a single gender-neutral route.
Purpose, admission, security, passport/document, residence, work, transit, extension and special-document conditions remain applicable.

policies.title: Other ordinary foreign passports: embassy visa or prior General Security approval
policies.summary: For countries not otherwise mentioned in its visa rules, General Security expressly requires an embassy visa or prior General Security authorisation; country-specific labour and other rules likewise require prior authorisation.
conditions: This explicit default excludes Lebanese citizenship, the Israel taxonomy-gap case, the GCC/Jordan border-visa cohort, the separately named automatic-tourism cohort, the Article Eight border-visa cohort, and the Egypt/Ghana/Iraq nationality-only ambiguities.

General Security labour-supplying-country rules require prior authorisation for named nationalities. Separate rules may offer conditional tourist, trader, doctor, engineer, business, GCC-resident, group, medical, conference, transit, diplomatic, official, service, work, student, or family routes; these do not alter the ordinary passport-only default.

Embassy applications require a passport valid at least six months, application, accommodation or invitation, return reservation, financial capability, profession evidence, and possibly residence evidence. General Security can request additional documents and the published procedure advises applying at least one month ahead.
Do not infer an eVisa from administrative processing. The source does not establish a generic self-service electronic visa.

policies.title: Armenian citizenship
policies.summary: An Armenian ordinary passport belongs to an Armenian citizen and is outside the foreign visitor-visa schedule.
conditions: Does not decide dual-national document choice, residence, work, exit, transit, security, or individual border treatment.

policies.title: Ordinary passports returned as visa-free by the live MFA checker
policies.summary: For an ordinary PASSPORT and tourism/relatives purpose, the current MFA E-Visa eligibility endpoint returns ALLOW_WITHOUT_VISA for these passports.
conditions: The checked route is ordinary PASSPORT (document type 167) and visitor purpose TOURISM_RELATIVES; it does not decide non-ordinary documents, work, residence, transit, or admission discretion.
The separate residence-permit programme is not this nationality-only result: it requires the stated six-month-valid qualifying permit and is active from 1 July 2026 to 1 July 2027.

policies.title: Ordinary passports returned as eVisa-eligible by the live MFA checker
policies.summary: For an ordinary PASSPORT and tourism/relatives purpose, the current MFA E-Visa eligibility endpoint returns ALLOWED_FOR_EVISA for these non-exempt, non-invitation-listed passports.
conditions: The live response is an advance electronic-visa route for ordinary PASSPORT and TOURISM_RELATIVES; it is not an arrival-visa classification even where a separate API field mentions border processing.

The temporary residence-permit exemption is conditional on a qualifying physical/sticker permit with at least six months' validity and ends 1 July 2027; it does not replace the passport-only baseline.

policies.title: Ordinary passports returned as consulate-only
policies.summary: The current MFA E-Visa eligibility endpoint returns ONLY_CONSULATE for these ordinary-passport tourism/relatives queries.
conditions: Sudan and Togo also appear on the MFA's published invitation-only list. Kosovo is consulate-only in the live checker but is not named on that list.
This is not a classification for diplomatic, official, service, refugee, alien, transit, residence, work, or case-specific documents and purposes.

policies.title: Iranian citizenship
policies.summary: An Iranian ordinary passport belongs to an Iranian citizen and is outside the foreign visitor-visa schedule.
conditions: Does not decide dual-national document choice, exit controls, residence, work, military service, or case-specific border treatment.

policies.title: Named ordinary passports: 15-day unilateral tourist exemption
policies.summary: The current Iranian MFA eVisa portal lists 27 ordinary-passport nationalities entitled to a unilateral tourism visa exemption.
conditions: Tourism only; the current MFA portal states one non-extendable 15-day stay in each six-month period.

The current portal says some visa types for some nationalities must be applied for in person and some nationalities may not be issued a visa for political or diplomatic reasons; it does not publish a complete passport-code schedule for those exceptions.

This policy does not establish work, residence, transit, diplomatic, official, service, emergency, refugee, alien-document, group-tour, sponsor, third-country-residence, security, or individual-admission treatment.

policies.title: Nine named foreign citizenships: visa-waiver rules
policies.summary: The current Iranian MFA eVisa portal identifies nine foreign citizenships as subject to Iran’s visa-waiver rules.
conditions: The portal describes these nationalities as subject to visa-waiver rules under internal laws, approvals, and bilateral agreements, but does not publish ordinary-passport stay length, purpose, entry point, passport-type, or recurrence terms.

This is a nationality-wide waiver classification only; it does not establish work, residence, diplomatic, official, service, refugee, emergency-document, transit, border-crossing, security, or individual-admission treatment.

policies.title: Lebanese, Venezuelan, and Malaysian nationals: permit at designated entry points
policies.summary: The current Iranian MFA eVisa portal says Lebanese, Venezuelan, and Malaysian nationals obtain necessary permits upon entry at designated entry points.
conditions: The portal calls the document a permit rather than a visa, but expressly makes it available upon entry at designated entry points. It is conservatively normalized as visa_on_arrival, not visa_free or eVisa.

Purpose, stay duration, document type, qualifying conditions, ports, security screening, and any prior approval are governed by the portal’s referenced established rules and conditions, which are not published as a code-level schedule.
This does not establish work, residence, diplomatic, official, service, emergency-document, transit, sponsor, security, or individual-admission treatment.

policies.title: Iraqi citizenship is outside foreign visitor-visa scope
policies.summary: An Iraqi ordinary passport belongs to an Iraqi citizen, whereas the federal Residence Law defines the visitor-visa regime for foreigners.
conditions: Does not decide a dual national’s document choice, residence, departure, security screening, consular treatment, or treatment when travelling on a foreign passport.

Article 1(Third)(h) separately excludes Iraqis and their children who hold foreign passports; that individual origin/document exception is not converted into a nationality-wide classification for every foreign passport code.

The federal law separately carves out heads of state, diplomatic and consular personnel, crew, authorized ship/plane/train passengers, treaty beneficiaries, minors on relatives’ passports, and neighboring-border residents. Those special-document, route, treaty, and residence facts are outside this ordinary-passport policy.

policies.title: Listed foreign ordinary passports: approved advance Visit Visa route
policies.summary: The current IPNA nationality eligibility dataset lists Visit Visa for every catalog passport code in this policy; the published route requires pre-travel approval and an embassy or consulate visa sticker, so it is normalized as visa_required rather than a true eVisa or a general visa on arrival.
conditions: The exact policy scope is the 196 catalog codes in the live eligibility dataset that display Visit Visa; Israel and Kosovo are deliberately excluded because neither appears in that dataset.

This is an online-portal application and approval workflow, but the published Visit Visa terms say the final visa sticker is issued by a Yemeni embassy or consulate abroad after Immigration, Passports and Nationality Authority approval; do not normalize it as eVisa.

For the published Visit Visa, an applicant needs a request from a Yemeni or foreign resident host able to accommodate and support the visitor and undertaking departure; round-trip tickets are required.

The portal requires the host request, a passport data page valid at least six months, an official health certificate showing no infectious disease, a departure undertaking, and documents for the stated purpose (kinship, treatment, study, or request).

The published Visit Visa terms do not state an initial permitted stay. They do not authorize work, residence, entry after denial, or admission despite security, health, document, or border-control concerns.

The portal separately publishes group-tourist and urgent-tourist routes. Group tourism requires accredited agencies and at least ten people; urgent tourist visas are granted as stickers at border crossings only after Authority approval and an accredited Yemeni tourism-agency request. Neither establishes nationality-wide ordinary visa-free or visa-on-arrival access.

The separate 72-hour transit visa requires onward nationality/residence or an onward entry visa plus confirmed travel. Crew, diplomatic/official, family, work, exit/re-entry, residence, and special visas have their own terms and are not generalized here.

The MFA announcement says the system connects Authority branches, official land, sea, and air ports and missions. It does not prove that every port is operational or that a route is accepted in every territory or by every de facto authority; this policy is limited to the Republic of Yemen/IPNA official service and official-port framework.

application.label: Yemen eVisa application portal
steps: Select the applicable Visit Visa route in the official portal and submit the host, passport, health, travel, departure, and purpose evidence.
Obtain Immigration, Passports and Nationality Authority approval and have the visa sticker issued by the relevant Yemeni embassy or consulate before travel.

policies.title: India: Indian citizens
policies.summary: Indian ordinary-passport holders are Indian citizens, not foreigners subject to the foreigner-visa rules.
conditions: Citizenship status only; it is not a finding about an overseas-citizenship card or a foreign passport held by a former Indian citizen.
Does not decide passport issuance, exit controls, dual-nationality questions, residence, work, transit, or admissibility.

policies.title: India: Nepalese and Bhutanese ordinary passports exempt on stated routes
policies.summary: The 2025 Exemption Order exempts Nepalese and Bhutanese citizens from the passport/visa requirement on their own-border routes, and on other stated routes when holding a valid passport.
conditions: The order covers entry by land or air over the Nepal or Bhutan border.
For entry from or to another place, the person must possess a valid passport; the order excludes travel from China, Macao, Hong Kong, or Pakistan from that limb.
Ordinary-passport nationality result only; do not generalize to diplomatic, official, service, transit, crew, residence, employment, security, protected-area, or case-specific admission.

policies.title: India: Maldivian ordinary passports exempt for short visits
policies.summary: India's current bilateral-relations brief describes bilateral visa-free tourism, medical and business entry for Maldives nationals for up to 90 days in the preceding six months.
conditions: For tourism, medical, and business purposes only; stay may not exceed 90 days in the preceding six months.
Valid passport/travel document and other applicable entry, security, health, admission, registration, protected-area, transit, crew, residence, work, and document rules remain applicable.
The separate diplomatic/official-passport waiver is outside this ordinary-passport policy.

policies.title: India: Japanese and South Korean ordinary passports eligible for visa on arrival
policies.summary: India Visa Online identifies Japanese and South Korean nationals for visa on arrival at six designated international airports.
conditions: Visitor must be visiting for no more than 60 days for business, tourism, conference, or medical purposes and meet the stated passport, funds, onward-ticket, admissibility, and other conditions.
Available only at Bengaluru, Chennai, Delhi, Hyderabad, Kolkata, and Mumbai international airports; it is non-extendable and non-convertible.
Not available to diplomatic/official-passport holders or persons of Pakistani origin (including the stated parent/grandparent or permanent-residence condition).
The UAE visa-on-arrival route is conditional on an earlier Indian eVisa or regular/paper visa and is therefore not a nationality-wide VOA classification; UAE remains in the eVisa policy.

application.label: India Visa Online: Visa on Arrival
steps: Complete the visa-on-arrival application and disembarkation form before or on arrival.
Present at a designated airport visa counter with the required passport, travel and financial evidence.
Pay the listed fee before the visa is granted.

policies.title: India: ordinary passports eligible for eVisa
policies.summary: The Bureau of Immigration's live eVisa portal lists these passport nationalities as eVisa-eligible; Japan and South Korea are kept in the easier visa-on-arrival policy.
conditions: Apply online, pay the eVisa fee, receive a granted ETA by email, print it, and present it at an eVisa-designated immigration check post.
For e-Tourist/e-Business applications, the portal says to apply at least four days before travel; an approved ETA is required before travelling.
Passport must generally have at least six months' validity; traveller needs onward/return travel and sufficient funds. Biometrics are captured on arrival.
eVisa is not available to diplomatic/official passports, laissez-passer or other non-passport travel documents, or persons endorsed on another person's passport.
Pakistani-passport holders or persons of Pakistani origin must apply for a regular visa at an Indian mission; this overrides nationality-list eligibility where applicable.

eVisa is non-extendable/non-convertible and not valid for protected, restricted, or cantonment areas without prior permission. It does not decide work, residence, transit outside the chosen eVisa category, crew, security, or admissibility.

application.label: India eVisa application
steps: Apply online and upload the required passport page, photograph, and category-specific documents.
Pay the country/territory-specific eVisa fee online.
Await a granted electronic travel authorization, then print it and present it at an eligible immigration check post.

policies.title: India: Afghan ordinary passports require an advance visa
policies.summary: India's central gateway routes Afghanistan nationals to a separate advance AFGHAN Visa service, whose published categories do not establish a standard e-Tourist visa.
conditions: The special portal publishes business, student, medical, medical-attendant, entry, and UN-diplomat services; it does not publish a standard e-Tourist category.
Its online form/ETA workflow is a special advance visa process, not evidence of the general eVisa route.

Purpose-specific documentation, prior authorization, security screening, passport validity, biometrics, registration, protected-area, transit, crew, residence, work, and admissibility conditions remain outside this nationality-only classification.

application.label: India AFGHAN Visa service
steps: Select the applicable published visa service and submit the online application.
Upload the passport bio page, national identity card, and purpose-specific documentation.
Wait for the visa/ETA decision before travelling.

policies.title: India: Pakistani ordinary passports require regular visa in advance
policies.summary: India's eVisa portal directs Pakistani-passport holders and persons of Pakistani origin to apply for a regular visa at an Indian mission.
conditions: The eVisa portal says Pakistani-passport holders and persons of Pakistani origin must apply for a regular visa at an Indian mission.

The current official gateway says all existing valid visas issued to Pakistani nationals, except medical, long-term, diplomatic and official visas, stood revoked immediately from 27 April 2025; medical visas were valid only until 29 April 2025. This record does not infer that a new ordinary visitor visa is presently grantable.
This is an advance regular/paper visa route, not eVisa or visa on arrival.
Purpose-specific, security, port, passport, registration, protected-area, transit, crew, residence, work, diplomatic/official-document, and admissibility conditions remain applicable.

application.label: India regular/paper visa application
steps: Complete the online regular-visa form.
Print and sign the form, then submit it with the passport and supporting documents to the appropriate Indian mission or visa application center.
Collect the passport and visa after the mission or center completes processing.

policies.title: India: other non-exempt ordinary passports require a regular visa in advance
policies.summary: Current Immigration and Foreigners Rules require an appropriate valid visa for foreign passports unless an express exemption applies; these nationalities are absent from the current eVisa eligibility list and ordinary-passport exemptions documented here.
conditions: The current rule requires an appropriate valid visa for foreign passport holders unless an express exemption applies; the central portal distinguishes regular/paper visa from limited-category eVisa.
Complete the online regular-visa form, then print/sign it and submit the passport and supporting documents to the relevant Indian mission or visa application center.

Do not use this policy for holders of an OCI/eOCI card, SAARC Visa Exemption/Visa Liberalisation Scheme endorsements, diplomatic/official/service passports, transit, crew, residence, work, protected/restricted-area travel, security or admission exceptions.

application.label: India regular/paper visa application
steps: Complete the online regular-visa application form.
Print and sign the application, then submit it with passport and supporting documents at the relevant Indian mission or visa application center.
Collect the passport and visa after processing.

policies.title: Sri Lankan citizenship is outside foreign visitor-visa scope
policies.summary: A Sri Lankan ordinary passport belongs to a Sri Lankan citizen and is not classified through the foreign short-visit ETA or visa framework.
conditions: Does not decide a dual national's document choice, departure, residence, security screening, or individual admissibility treatment.

policies.title: 43 named ordinary passports: fee-waived Tourist ETA
policies.summary: From 25 May 2026, 40 named nationalities plus Maldives, Seychelles, and Singapore receive a fee-waived Tourist ETA. It remains an ETA requirement, not visa-free access.
conditions: The 40-country scheme expressly covers ordinary passports as well as diplomatic, official, and service passports. Singapore, Seychelles, and Maldives have reciprocal arrangements; ordinary Maldivian passports receive 90 days, while the other named free-ETA passports receive 30 days.

The free Tourist ETA permits double entry from first arrival within the 30-day validity period; on a second entry, only the balance of the 30 days is granted. A fee is due for an extension beyond 30 days.

The Department states that all foreign nationals, including the 40 fee-waiver nationalities and Maldives, Seychelles, and Singapore, require an ETA before arrival; this policy therefore does not treat a waived fee as visa-free entry.

Apply electronically through the official ETA portal. The ETA must be used to enter within three months of issue; tourist ETA is initially up to 30 days from arrival and may be extended up to six months.

At entry, ETA holders need a passport valid at least six months from arrival, a confirmed return ticket, and sufficient funds. ETA is not admission; false information, security/admissibility findings, or a referral can result in refusal.

ETA holders must not undertake paid or unpaid employment, trade, or business beyond the granted ETA purpose. Residence, work, longer stay, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service, UN, special-document and diplomatic-mission rules are separate.

The official application page retains a limited BIA-only, additional-fee ETA-on-arrival facility for travellers without prior approval. It remains an approval-contingent airport fallback, not a nationality-wide visa-free rule; the published standard is ETA before travel.

A different live ETA subpage still says Singapore, Maldives, and Seychelles are ETA-exempt for short visits. The current Department notice and current ETA overview expressly say these same nationalities require ETA, so this policy follows the later current notice/overview and records the disagreement for review.

application.label: Sri Lanka ETA application
steps: Submit the Tourist ETA application and required traveller details through the official portal before travel.
Keep the ETA approval and meet passport-validity, onward-ticket, funds, purpose, and admissibility requirements at entry.

policies.title: Five named ordinary passports: sponsor-submitted ETA
policies.summary: Afghanistan, Cameroon, Côte d'Ivoire, Ghana, and Nigeria may apply for ETA through a Sri Lankan sponsor at the Department head office, rather than receiving an unrestricted online ordinary-visitor outcome.
conditions: A Sri Lankan sponsor must submit the request, sponsor affidavit, certified sponsor ID/passport copy, applicant police-clearance report, applicant passport copy, and accommodation proof to the Department head office for consideration.
This is an advance, sponsor-mediated ETA route. The alert identifies this special process but does not independently state the nationality scope of the BIA limited facility.

The Department states that all foreign nationals, including the 40 fee-waiver nationalities and Maldives, Seychelles, and Singapore, require an ETA before arrival; this policy therefore does not treat a waived fee as visa-free entry.
The sponsor-submitted ETA must be used to enter within three months of issue; tourist ETA is initially up to 30 days from arrival and may be extended up to six months.

At entry, ETA holders need a passport valid at least six months from arrival, a confirmed return ticket, and sufficient funds. ETA is not admission; false information, security/admissibility findings, or a referral can result in refusal.

ETA holders must not undertake paid or unpaid employment, trade, or business beyond the granted ETA purpose. Residence, work, longer stay, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service, UN, special-document and diplomatic-mission rules are separate.

The official application page retains a limited BIA-only, additional-fee ETA-on-arrival facility for travellers without prior approval. It remains an approval-contingent airport fallback, not a nationality-wide visa-free rule; the published standard is ETA before travel.

application.label: Sri Lanka ETA portal and restricted-nationality notice
steps: Arrange for a Sri Lankan sponsor to lodge the required documents at the Department of Immigration and Emigration head office.
Await consideration and ETA approval before travel; the special alert does not establish this sponsor route as an airport process.

policies.title: Other ordinary passports: standard short-visit ETA
policies.summary: The current Department default requires a standard ETA for every other catalog foreign ordinary-passport code; the source does not create a nationality-wide visa-free complement.
conditions: The Department states that all foreign nationals, including the 40 fee-waiver nationalities and Maldives, Seychelles, and Singapore, require an ETA before arrival; this policy therefore does not treat a waived fee as visa-free entry.

Apply electronically through the official ETA portal. The ETA must be used to enter within three months of issue; tourist ETA is initially up to 30 days from arrival and may be extended up to six months.

At entry, ETA holders need a passport valid at least six months from arrival, a confirmed return ticket, and sufficient funds. ETA is not admission; false information, security/admissibility findings, or a referral can result in refusal.

ETA holders must not undertake paid or unpaid employment, trade, or business beyond the granted ETA purpose. Residence, work, longer stay, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service, UN, special-document and diplomatic-mission rules are separate.

The official application page retains a limited BIA-only, additional-fee ETA-on-arrival facility for travellers without prior approval. It remains an approval-contingent airport fallback, not a nationality-wide visa-free rule; the published standard is ETA before travel.

application.label: Sri Lanka ETA application
steps: Submit the short-visit ETA application electronically before travel and await approval or a referral notice.
Carry the ETA approval and the required valid passport, return ticket, and funds to the port of entry.

policies.title: Vietnamese citizenship is outside foreign visitor-visa scope
policies.summary: A Vietnamese ordinary passport belongs to a Vietnamese citizen and is not classified through the foreigner eVisa or foreign visitor-exemption framework.
conditions: Does not decide a dual national’s document choice, overseas-Vietnamese visa-exemption certificate, residence, departure, security, or individual admissibility treatment.

policies.title: Twelve nationalities: Resolution 44 unilateral visa exemption
policies.summary: The current Resolution 44 policy exempts these nationals from visas for a 45-day stay, regardless of passport type or entry purpose.
conditions: Applies to Germany, France, Italy, Spain, the United Kingdom, Russia, Japan, South Korea, Denmark, Sweden, Norway, and Finland, regardless of passport type and entry purpose.

Requires full compliance with Vietnam’s legal entry conditions. The current MOFA table states unilateral-exemption entrants need a passport valid at least six months and at least 30 days outside Viet Nam since their last departure.
British National (Overseas) passport holders are expressly excluded by the MOFA table; this ordinary UK-passport policy does not cover BNO or other special British documents.
Work, residence, overseas-Vietnamese, diplomatic/official, transit, crew, and individual security/admissibility rules remain separate.

policies.title: Twelve nationalities: Resolution 229 visa exemption
policies.summary: The current Resolution 229 policy exempts these nationals from visas for up to 45 days from entry, regardless of passport type, subject to legal entry conditions.
conditions: Applies to Belgium, Bulgaria, Croatia, Czechia, Hungary, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Poland, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, and Switzerland, regardless of passport type.

Maximum stay is 45 days from entry and remains subject to Vietnam’s legal entry conditions. The current MOFA table states unilateral-exemption entrants need a passport valid at least six months and at least 30 days outside Viet Nam since their last departure.
This current 2025-2028 resolution supersedes the expired 2025 Poland/Czechia/Switzerland package-tour pilot for the same ordinary passports; do not retain the expired tour-only condition.
Work, residence, overseas-Vietnamese, diplomatic/official, transit, crew, and individual security/admissibility rules remain separate.

policies.title: Belarus ordinary passports: reciprocal visa exemption
policies.summary: Belarus ordinary-passport holders are visa-exempt for up to 30 days per stay, capped at 90 days in a calendar year.
conditions: The current MOFA table records 30 days for all passport types and caps ordinary-passport stay at 90 days in a calendar year.
The ordinary-passport agreement is distinct from diplomatic/official rules; purpose, work, residence, security, and admission limitations remain governed by Vietnamese law.

policies.title: Brunei ordinary passports: 14-day visa exemption
policies.summary: Brunei ordinary-passport holders are visa-exempt for stays up to 14 days.
conditions: The current MOFA table distinguishes 14 days for ordinary Brunei passports from 30 days for diplomatic and official passports.
Does not establish work, residence, diplomatic/official, transit, crew, special-document, security, or individual-admission rights.

policies.title: Ten ordinary passports: bilateral short-stay visa exemptions
policies.summary: These current bilateral instruments give ordinary-passport holders short-stay visa exemption, with duration and purpose conditions varying by nationality.
conditions: Cambodia, Indonesia, Kyrgyzstan, Laos, Malaysia, Mongolia, Myanmar, Singapore, and Thailand have 30-day ordinary-passport routes; Kazakhstan is 30 days per entry, capped at 90 days in each 180-day period.

The current MOFA instrument schedule records: Cambodia effective 5 December 2008 (amended 1 January 2010); Indonesia 4 December 2003; Kazakhstan 25 May 2024; Laos 1 July 2004; Malaysia 25 November 2001; Myanmar 26 October 2013 (amended 1 January 2020); Mongolia 6 March 2024; Singapore 1 December 2003; and Thailand 9 July 2000. It identifies Kyrgyzstan as a successor arrangement with the former Soviet agreement, without printing an effective date.

Cambodia, Indonesia, Kazakhstan, Laos, Mongolia, Myanmar, and Singapore require at least six months' passport validity. Mongolia, Myanmar, and Singapore exclude income-earning activity; Myanmar also excludes other commercial activity. Malaysia is limited to the listed short-visit purposes; Laos and Indonesia have separate extension/residence rules.

The MOFA table separately records ordinary-passport periods for these bilateral arrangements. Do not generalize diplomatic, official, service, special, crew, ASEAN-official-event, residence, or border-pass rows to ordinary visitor passports.

policies.title: Philippines ordinary passports: 21-day visa exemption
policies.summary: Philippines ordinary-passport holders are visa-exempt for stays up to 21 days when they hold a passport valid at least six months and an onward or return ticket.
conditions: The current MOFA table records an ordinary-passport exemption of up to 21 days, requiring a passport valid at least six months and a return or onward ticket.
The table separately identifies diplomatic, official, ASEAN-official-event, work, residence, special-document, security, and individual-admission provisions; they are not generalized here.

policies.title: Chile and Panama ordinary passports: 90-day non-remunerated-activity exemptions
policies.summary: Chile and Panama ordinary-passport holders are visa-exempt for stays up to 90 days when entry is not for income-earning activity.
conditions: The MOFA table records 90-day ordinary-passport exemption for Chile and Panama; the underlying ordinary-passport rules require passports valid at least six months and prohibit entry for income-earning activity.
Do not generalize the diplomatic/official/special, crew, residence, employment, or individual security/admission provisions.

policies.title: Other foreign ordinary passports: all-nationalities eVisa
policies.summary: Every other catalog foreign ordinary-passport code can use Vietnam’s nationality-wide electronic-visa route; it is normalized as evisa.
conditions: Available to foreigners outside Viet Nam holding a valid passport or international travel document. The Article 8 visa-class and Article 16 invitation/guarantee rules, including their personal, delegation, diplomatic, residence, and purpose distinctions, remain separate procedures rather than nationality-wide ordinary-passport exclusions.

Valid for at most 90 days, for single or multiple entry. The Ministry of Public Security states that application, issuance, receipt, printing, and fee payment are electronic; an issued eVisa can be printed without collecting a visa at a mission or border gate.

Use only Government-designated international air, land, or sea border gates. The Government Portal confirms the official site publishes the eVisa border-gate list; the pre-arrival declaration is not an ETA or visa-exemption substitute.

Entry and stay remain conditioned on a valid travel document, the stated entry purpose, no suspension/prohibition from entry, and border-control admission. Accommodation providers must make temporary-residence declarations; work, residence, diplomatic/official, crew, border-pass, transit and overseas-Vietnamese certificate routes are distinct.

application.label: Viet Nam E-Visa
steps: Apply personally from outside Viet Nam, accurately complete the eVisa form, and select approved entry/exit border gates.
Pay the non-refundable eVisa fee and receive the result electronically before travel.
Enter and exit only at the designated border gates and comply with temporary-residence declaration and border-control requirements.

policies.title: Thailand: Thai ordinary-passport holders
policies.summary: Thai citizens are not foreign nationals subject to Thailand's foreign-national visa and TDAC requirement.
conditions: Citizenship classification only; it does not determine dual-nationality, passport issuance, exit controls, residence, work, transit, or admissibility.
A Thai citizen travelling on a foreign passport is outside this passport-nationality finding.

policies.title: Thailand: current 60-day ordinary-passport visa exemption
policies.summary: The current Consular Affairs schedule gives these ordinary-passport nationalities visa-exempt admission for tourism and short-term business engagements for up to 60 days.
conditions: For tourism and short-term business engagements only, with a stay not exceeding 60 days.

The current schedule is used because it remains linked by the 31 March 2026 Consular Affairs index. The 19 May 2026 revision notice says its changes begin only 15 days after a Ministry of Interior announcement appears in the Royal Gazette; recheck before travel.
TDAC must be submitted by non-Thai nationals up to three days before arrival; it is an arrival declaration, not a visa or ETA.
Does not establish work, residence, transit, crew, diplomatic/official/special-document, border-pass, extension, repeat-entry, security, or discretionary-admission rights.

policies.title: Thailand: 14-day bilateral ordinary-passport visa exemption
policies.summary: Myanmar and Timor-Leste ordinary-passport holders have the listed 14-day bilateral visa-exemption route.
conditions: Maximum stay is 14 days.
For Myanmar, the schedule expressly limits the route to international airports.
TDAC applies to non-Thai arrivals and is not a visa or ETA.
No inference for work, residence, transit, crew, diplomatic/official/special documents, border passes, extensions, repeat entry, or discretionary admission.

policies.title: Thailand: 30-day bilateral ordinary-passport visa exemption
policies.summary: Chile's ordinary-passport bilateral agreement provides a 30-day visa-exemption route.
conditions: Maximum stay is 30 days.
TDAC applies to non-Thai arrivals and is not a visa or ETA.
No inference for work, residence, transit, crew, diplomatic/official/special documents, border passes, extensions, repeat entry, or discretionary admission.

policies.title: Thailand: 90-day bilateral ordinary-passport visa exemption
policies.summary: Argentina and Brazil ordinary-passport bilateral agreements provide a 90-day visa-exemption route.
conditions: Maximum stay is 90 days.
TDAC applies to non-Thai arrivals and is not a visa or ETA.
No inference for work, residence, transit, crew, diplomatic/official/special documents, border passes, extensions, repeat entry, or discretionary admission.

policies.title: Thailand: 15-day ordinary-passport visa on arrival
policies.summary: The current Consular Affairs VOA schedule gives these ordinary-passport nationalities a 15-day visa-on-arrival route; entries with the concurrent 60-day exemption are classified under that easier route instead.
conditions: The schedule states a 15-day stay. It does not establish a nationality-wide electronic visa, ETA, or advance-visa requirement for these passports.

TDAC applies to non-Thai arrivals and is not a visa or ETA.
No inference for work, residence, transit, crew, diplomatic/official/special documents, border passes, security, or discretionary admission.

policies.title: Thailand: foreign ordinary passports eligible to apply for Thai eVisa
policies.summary: The MFA says foreign nationals can apply for Thai eVisa worldwide except from inside Thailand. These passports have no easier nationality-wide route established by the current schedules above.
conditions: Applicant must be a foreign national located outside Thailand; the worldwide statement establishes availability of the electronic application route, not guaranteed issuance or admission.

The portal requires an online account, application, supporting documents and payment. The competent mission may seek further documents or interview the applicant; exact visa type, purpose, document and nationality checks remain case-specific.
TDAC applies to non-Thai arrivals and is an arrival declaration, not a visa or ETA.

This ordinary-passport visitor-route classification does not establish work, residence, transit, crew, diplomatic/official/special-document, border-pass, fee, duration, port, extension, security, or discretionary-admission rights.

application.label: Thai eVisa official portal
steps: Apply from outside Thailand through the Thai eVisa portal.
Create an account, select the appropriate visa category, upload the required documents, and pay the stated fee.
Await the competent mission's decision and use the approval email as instructed for travel and Immigration inspection.

policies.title: Philippines: Philippine ordinary-passport holders
policies.summary: A valid Philippine passport is citizenship proof for Philippine arrival processing, rather than a foreign visitor-visa route.
conditions: This is a same-country citizenship normalization only; it does not determine dual nationality, passport issuance, exit controls, residence, work, transit, security, or any foreign passport held by the person.
The cited BI order also covers retained or reacquired Philippine citizens travelling with a foreign passport and specified proof; that conditional route is not inferred from a foreign passport code.

policies.title: Philippines: EO 408 30-day ordinary-passport visa-free entry
policies.summary: The current DFA eVisa policy gives these ordinary-passport nationalities visa-free temporary entry for business or tourism for up to 30 days.
conditions: For business or tourism temporary visits only, initially not exceeding 30 days.
Traveller must hold a passport valid at least six months beyond the contemplated stay and a return or onward ticket.
Brazil and Israel have the separately stated 59-day arrangement; Brunei and Cambodia are separated due to a live official-service duration conflict.
eTravel is an arrival/departure declaration that replaced cards; it is not normalized as an ETA or visa.

policies.title: Other foreign ordinary passports: advance consular visa required
policies.summary: After its current named visa-free and simplified/eVisa cohorts, the MFA PDF expressly says citizens of all other countries must obtain a visa from Tajik embassies or consulates before departure.
conditions: This is an explicit official default for other foreign countries, not an inference from their absence in an eVisa list. Obtain the visa from a Tajik embassy or consulate before departure.

The classification does not collapse the separate support-confirmation/official-invitation simplified arrival process into a nationality-wide visa on arrival. It also does not claim that online submission converts a consular visa into eVisa issuance.
Registration, passport validity, purpose, duration, entries, port, fee, supporting documents, extension, onward travel, funds, security and individual-admissibility requirements remain applicable.
Does not decide GBAO permits, residence, work, business, transit, diplomatic, official, service, special-document, stateless-person, PRC travel-document or route-specific treatment.

policies.title: Tajikistan: citizenship entry
policies.summary: Tajikistan's Constitution gives a citizen the right to travel, leave the Republic and return, supporting the same-country citizenship classification.
conditions: This is a citizenship/right-of-return finding, not foreign visitor-visa evidence.
It does not decide documentary requirements, dual nationality, residence, GBAO access, exit control, security, criminal-law or individual-admissibility issues.

policies.title: Turkmenistan: citizen right of entry
policies.summary: Turkmenistan’s Migration Law and current Migration Service guidance directly establish a Turkmen citizen’s right to enter with the prescribed citizen travel document.
conditions: The current Migration Service identifies the biometric Turkmen passport as an entry document; the Migration Law establishes the citizen entry right. This is not a foreign visitor visa exemption.
This does not decide dual-nationality/document choice, exit restrictions, residence, work, military, registration, security or individual border treatment.

policies.title: United States ordinary passports: tourism visa exemption
policies.summary: Current official traveller guidance expressly identifies United States nationals as subject to a visa-exemption arrangement when travelling for tourism.
conditions: The exemption is expressly stated for tourism. It does not establish visa-free business, work, residence, transit, study, media, volunteer, diplomatic, official, service or special-document access.

The statement appears in current air-or-sea arrival guidance. It does not independently establish a separate land-border entitlement or remove normal documentary, health, security and individual-admissibility checks.
The statutory 30-day tourist-visa duration does not itself specify the stay length of the exemption; comply with the entry permission actually granted and any current Immigration conditions.

policies.title: Other foreign ordinary passports: Dili airport or seaport visa on arrival
policies.summary: The current Customs Authority page states that nationals of other countries may apply for a visa on arrival only at Dili International Airport or Dili Sea Port. This residual policy excludes the operative EU–Timor-Leste waiver cohort.
conditions: For every listed foreign passport not separately exempt, the current ordinary visitor route is a visa application on arrival only at Dili International Airport or Dili Sea Port. This policy is not a nationwide or land-border VOA finding.

Indonesian nationals may apply on arrival at any border post, including land crossings, Dili International Airport and Dili Sea Port. All other listed passports arriving at a land border must first obtain a Visa Application Authorization, present it to Immigration, and then receive a visa on payment; this advance-authorisation route is not normalized as eVisa or an unrestricted VOA.

The current page requires an arrivals card, genuine tourist or business purpose, sufficient funds, accommodation arrangements, a travel document valid at least six months with an unused visa page, onward/return arrangements, and USD 30 cash. Immigration may refuse applicants who do not meet requirements.
The Act gives tourist visas a 30-day validity, single entry, and one equal extension; a trip to or from Oe-Cusse Ambeno permits multiple entries. Tourist visas do not authorize professional activity.

Does not decide residence, work, business class II, transit, airport-transit, Oe-Cusse border-pass, visa-support/advance mission procedure, diplomatic, official, service, special-document, citizenship, security, health, criminal-history or case-specific admission treatment.

policies.title: EU ordinary passports: reciprocal short-stay visa waiver
policies.summary: The operative EU–Timor-Leste agreement waives a Timor-Leste visa for ordinary passports of EU Member States except Ireland, and takes precedence over bilateral arrangements within its scope.
conditions: Valid ordinary passport; stays in Timor-Leste may not exceed 90 days in any 180-day period.
Paid activity is excluded. The agreement does not establish work, residence, long-stay, diplomatic, official, service or special-document treatment.
The waiver applies regardless of transport mode. Entry and short-stay conditions, individual refusal, and other admissibility requirements remain applicable.
The EU agreement takes precedence over bilateral agreements or arrangements on matters it covers; the Customs page's narrower named list does not displace this operative treaty cohort.

policies.title: Timor-Leste: citizenship entry
policies.summary: The Immigration and Asylum Act expressly regulates the entry and exit conditions of Timor-Leste nationals separately from foreigners, supporting the same-country citizenship classification.
conditions: This is a nationality/citizenship classification, not foreign visitor-visa evidence.
It does not decide passport issuance, dual nationality, exit controls, residence, land-border documents, security, criminal-law or individual-admissibility issues.

policies.title: Non-calling ordinary passports: Indonesia C1 electronic tourist visitor visa
policies.summary: For the listed formerly unresolved ordinary passports, the central Directorate's current C1 rule establishes an account-based, pre-travel electronic visitor-visa route without a sponsor. Nationalities affected by either currently published Calling Visa schedule, and Kosovo whose portal mapping was not disclosed, remain unresolved.
conditions: This policy applies only to holders of a national ordinary passport who were unresolved in the promoted Indonesia batch and are absent from both currently published Calling Visa schedules. It does not duplicate BVK, VOA/e-VOA, or Indonesian-citizen policies.

C1 is a single-entry visitor visa for tourism, personal development, tourist-attraction study, cruise travel, selected MICE participation, business discussions/negotiation/site visits, medical-related activities, and the listed non-work activities. It grants an initial stay of up to 60 days, may be extended up to 180 days, and cannot be used to sell goods or services or receive Indonesian work compensation.

The Directorate's C1 page directs applicants to the official eVisa service for account-based application with electronic files; the official portal says an approved visa is downloadable from a link sent by email. This is an available electronic pre-travel route, not a visa on arrival.

The current materials require a passport valid at least six months, recent photograph, and evidence of at least USD 2,000 living expenses; the visa is valid for 90 days after issuance if unused. Admission and any stay permit remain subject to Immigration assessment.

The live eVisa selection page exposes Passport/Country/Region fields but did not disclose individual country results in this review. Recheck the mutable selector before promotion or travel. The central C1 page expressly says no sponsor, but an undated regional C1 page retains sponsor-led template instructions; the central Directorate page is treated as controlling, while this operational inconsistency remains a material risk.

A second official regional schedule currently identifies Cameroon, Guinea and Niger as Calling Visa nationals while the Bontang schedule does not. Those three codes are left unresolved rather than treated as a no-sponsor complement.

application.label: Indonesia Directorate General of Immigration eVisa service
application.processingTime: The C1 page states five working days after payment for Directorate or representative processing.
steps: Use the official eVisa service referenced by the Directorate General of Immigration C1 page to submit the C1 pre-travel application and electronic files.
Provide a national passport valid at least six months, recent photograph, and required evidence of funds; pay the billed C1 fee after the application is accepted.
Wait for the visa decision before travel and present the approved C1 and required travel documents for immigration examination on arrival.

policies.title: Ten named ordinary passports: Cambodia advance Tourist Visa T
policies.summary: The current Cambodian Embassy visitor guidance expressly requires these named ordinary passport holders to obtain their entry visa before departure; it does not establish a nationality-wide eVisa or visa-on-arrival route for them.
conditions: The official Embassy list names Afghanistan, Algeria, Saudi Arabia, Bangladesh, Iran, Iraq, Pakistan, Sri Lanka, Sudan and Nigeria as passports for which an entry visa before departure must be issued by the Embassy. This is an advance visa classification, not an eVisa or visa on arrival finding.

Tourist Visa T is single entry, valid for three months from issue, permits a 30-day stay, and cannot be changed or used for employment. Its extension and any other purpose or residence route are outside this baseline.

The page requires a passport valid for six months after departure from Cambodia; the Embassy's prior-visa application also asks for travel, accommodation and residence documentation. Admission and visa issuance remain discretionary.
Cambodia e-Arrival is a separate immigration, health and customs declaration. It may be submitted within seven days before or on arrival and does not convert this route into an ETA or eVisa.

This policy concerns national ordinary passports only. It does not establish Visa E/business, group, transit, diplomatic, official, service, courtesy, K-visa/Khmer-origin, refugee, alien or other special-document treatment.

policies.title: Named ordinary passports: visa-free short visitors
policies.summary: The official Washington Embassy's full current named visa-free schedule supports this reconcilable ordinary-passport cohort. Passports disputed by the current statutory Tourism Organisation schedule are excluded.
conditions: The Embassy lists this cohort among countries whose citizens do not require a visa. It does not establish visa-free work, residence, business, transit, diplomatic, official, service, special-document or individual-admissibility treatment.

Government guidance requires a passport valid at least six months in the absence of a specific bilateral agreement, caps visitor stays at 90 days in each calendar year, and says extensions are available from Immigration.
No general arrival authorization or visa-on-arrival status is inferred. Border officials may apply normal documentary, health, security and admission controls.

policies.title: Named ordinary passports: advance online tourist visa
policies.summary: The official Washington Embassy required-country schedule, supplemented for Marshall Islands by the statutory Tourism Organisation's required list, establishes a visitor visa requirement. The Department of Immigration makes the tourist application available online through the official eVisa portal and at missions; it is normalized as an advance eVisa route.
conditions: Submit the tourism-visa application before travel through the official eVisa portal, or at an Immigration office, Botswana mission or consulate. The Department says online approval/rejection is accessed in the portal.

An online-approved traveller may travel with the approval letter as proof of the visa; Immigration prints the visa at the airport or other port of entry. This post-approval printing is not a nationality-wide visa-on-arrival finding.

The Government page says the service takes 7–14 working days. A tourism visa is for recreational travel, with a single entry up to one month or multiple entry up to three months; it does not authorize work, residence, business-only, transit, diplomatic, official, service or special-document treatment.

The application requires a passport valid at least six months, photographs, covering letter, flight and accommodation itinerary, trip itinerary and intention to depart; a re-entry permit may be required for the country of residence. Approval and admission remain discretionary.

Government visitor information caps visitors at 90 days in each calendar year and permits extensions through Immigration. The cited nationality schedules lack effective dates and include obsolete or inconsistent country labels; the eVisa frontend is dated 2021 and did not yield selector evidence. Reconfirm directly with Immigration before travel or promotion.

application.label: Botswana Government eVisa service
application.processingTime: Government tourism-visa guidance states 7–14 working days after application.
steps: Apply online through the official Botswana eVisa service before travel, or submit Form 1 at Immigration or a Botswana mission or consulate.
Upload the stated passport, photographs, purpose, itinerary, accommodation and onward-departure evidence; supply any required residence-country re-entry documentation.
Wait for approval before travel, carry the approval letter and supporting documents, and complete Immigration examination and visa printing at the port of entry.

policies.title: Albania ordinary passports: 30-day visa-free regime
policies.summary: The MFA eVisa selector's country-specific live backend response directly identifies Albania's ordinary-passport visa-free regime as up to 30 days.
conditions: The result is an ordinary-passport baseline and records a stay of up to 30 days.
It does not establish work, residence, registration, transit, diplomatic, official, service or special-document treatment; normal entry and individual-admissibility checks remain applicable.
The response also labels a facilitated visa regime, but that label does not by itself identify a tourist eVisa route and is not normalized here.

policies.title: Thailand ordinary passports: 30-day visa-free regime
policies.summary: The MFA eVisa selector's country-specific live backend response directly identifies Thailand's ordinary-passport visa-free regime as up to 30 days.
conditions: The result is an ordinary-passport baseline and records a stay of up to 30 days.
