Present the ETA and supporting documents for Immigration examination.

policies.title: Ghana: other ordinary passports — advance electronic visitor visa
policies.summary: For every remaining foreign catalog passport, the live official checker returns 'Visa Required' with eVisa authorization and an electronic application path. This is a true advance eVisa route, not a conclusion from online-form availability alone.
conditions: The official checker explicitly returns eVisa authorization and an application route for this cohort; embassy processing is presented as an alternative, so the easier electronic route is normalized as eVisa.

The official portal states tourist visits include holidays, visiting friends or family and short-term recreation up to three months. Single-entry visas are valid for 90 days from issuance; this is validity to travel, not a promise of a three-month admission period.

The portal requires a passport valid at least six months beyond intended stay, photograph, travel details and purpose-dependent supporting documents such as invitation/business letters. Yellow-fever, fees, onward travel, accommodation, security, admissibility, port examination and any extension rules remain applicable.

Emergency visas at entry require absence of a Ghanaian mission and advance Director authorization through a sponsor; that case-specific contingency is not a nationality-wide visa-on-arrival policy. This policy excludes work, residence, business-only, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service and special-document routes.

application.label: Ghana Official eVisa Application Portal
application.processingTime: The public portal advertises standard processing of 96 hours; individual approval and admission are not guaranteed.
steps: Check the nationality result in the official portal.
Create an account and submit the tourist eVisa application with passport, photograph, travel and supporting documents.
Receive and carry the approved electronic visa before travel, then satisfy Immigration examination at entry.

policies.title: Ghana: Ghanaian citizenship entry
policies.summary: The live official eligibility checker returns Ghanaian citizens as requiring no authorization, supporting the same-country citizenship classification.
conditions: The source supports only that a Ghanaian citizen does not require visitor authorization. It does not decide documentary, dual-nationality, residence, border, security or individual-admissibility questions.

policies.title: Tanzanian citizens: outside foreign-visitor visa regime
policies.summary: The Immigration Department's current entry guidance distinguishes Tanzanian citizens from foreign nationals subject to visa or visa-on-arrival procedures. The same-country ordinary-passport pair is therefore recorded as citizenship rather than a foreign visitor visa status.
conditions: All travellers must use designated formal entry points, appear to an immigration officer, complete the arrival declaration and produce a passport or other acceptable document.
This does not decide citizenship acquisition, dual nationality, passport validity, residence, customs, health, security, criminal process or individual border formalities.

policies.title: Named ordinary passports: Tanzania visa-free visitors
policies.summary: The 2016 Visa Regulations' Third Schedule directly names 44 of this cohort as not requiring a visa. Current eVisa group guidance directly supports the two additional EAC/SADC entries (CD and ZW); the separate detailed eVisa-list URL was unavailable on re-review, so no wider unlisted complement is inferred.
conditions: This policy applies only to the directly supported ordinary-passport cohort. It does not establish a common stay limit, work entitlement, residence right, transit rule or special-document exemption.

The current eVisa guide's broad EAC/SADC/Commonwealth wording conflicts with its own detailed VOA/referral categories and with portions of the 2016 schedules. The current detailed visa-free endpoint returned a runtime error on re-review. The 44 statutory Third-Schedule codes are retained; CD and ZW are the only additional catalog codes directly supported by the current EAC/SADC wording and not contradicted by a current named route. Burundi and South Sudan remain unresolved because they are omitted from the statutory schedule and all current detailed categories despite the EAC prose.

All entry remains through designated points with a passport or other acceptable document, arrival declaration, and possible onward-travel, funds and current health/yellow-fever documentation. The Immigration Officer retains admission authority.

policies.title: Named ordinary passports: Tanzania ordinary or multiple visa on arrival
policies.summary: The current official Immigration guideline expressly gives this named cohort both online and visa-on-arrival facilities. Because the same visitor visa can be issued at an official entry point, the easiest supported baseline is visa_on_arrival, not evisa.
conditions: The direct named schedule grants both online and on-arrival facilities. It does not make an online application mandatory, so this is not normalized as evisa. Issuance is only at an official designated entry point, not an assertion that every port offers an arrival visa.

An ordinary tourist visa is stated to cost USD 50 and be valid up to 90 days. United States passport holders visiting for tourism are instead required to use the USD 100 multiple visa, even for a single entry; the guide nevertheless includes the United States in the named on-arrival cohort.

The portal's raw lists overlap: Ghana, Saint Lucia and Saint Vincent are also on the live visa-free schedule, so their direct no-visa route prevails; Burkina Faso and Guinea appear in the raw VOA list but are referral cases, so the referral eVisa policy prevails. These codes are omitted from this VOA policy.

Ordinary visa holders may not work or conduct business. Transit, work, residence, business-only, diplomatic, official, service, refugee/stateless, special-document and Zanzibar-specific operating rules are not decided by this policy. Entry remains subject to documents, health, funds/onward travel and officer discretion.

application.label: Tanzania Immigration eVisa service
application.processingTime: The terms say online applications should be lodged ten days before expected travel; this does not apply where the visitor instead uses the expressly available on-arrival route.
steps: Choose either the official online visa application or the permitted visa-on-arrival procedure at an official entry point.
For an online application, submit the required documents and payment, then obtain the Visa Grant Notice through the portal before travel.
Present the required documents to Immigration. A grant notice or arrival-visa application does not guarantee admission.

policies.title: Referral ordinary passports: Tanzania advance electronic visa approval
policies.summary: Tanzania Immigration's current referral list prohibits this cohort from using visa on arrival without special Commissioner-General permission and requires an online application approved before travel. The online grant notice makes the ordinary baseline evisa.
conditions: Referral nationals must apply online and wait for approval before starting travel, unless they obtain special approval from the Commissioner General of Immigration. They are advised to apply at least two months before travel and supply local-host/contact and invitation or visa-application-letter information where available.

This policy is evisa because the official portal processes the online application and lets approved applicants download the Visa Grant Notice. It does not turn the exceptional Commissioner's permission into a nationality-wide VOA route.

The direct referral list takes precedence over the raw VOA schedule's Burkina Faso and Guinea entries. Refugee and stateless applicants also cannot use VOA but are document/status categories, not ordinary-passport nationality policies.

Ordinary visitor approval does not authorize work or business and remains subject to entry documents, designated ports, health/yellow-fever requirements, funds/onward evidence, security and immigration-officer discretion.

application.label: Tanzania Immigration referral visa application
application.processingTime: Referral applicants are advised to submit at least two months before travel and must wait for approval before commencing the journey.
steps: Submit the referral visa application through the official Tanzania Immigration portal.
Provide the passport, supporting documents, local-host details and an invitation or visa-application letter addressed to the Commissioner General where available.
Wait for approval, download the Visa Grant Notice from the portal, and present it with entry documents at a designated entry point.

policies.title: Named ordinary passports: visa-free visitor entry
policies.summary: The current Government Tourism arrangements expressly designate this ordinary-passport cohort Visa Free. The broader SADC and COMESA wording remains subject to reciprocity, so only the page's explicit named-country outcomes are normalized.
conditions: The Tourism page says visa exemption is subject to reciprocity and may change. This is an ordinary-passport short-visitor classification only, not a finding on work, residence, business-only, study, transit, diplomatic, official, service, refugee or other special-document travel.

The page's named Visa-Exempt Countries section includes Dominica although its detailed country grid omits a Dominica row. It is retained as directly named visa-free evidence, but that internal presentation gap is a material review risk.

The official High Commission's dated 2024 79-country waiver announcement names examples that differ from the current 2026 schedules. It is retained as historical reconciliation evidence only, not expanded into a present-day default without a current authoritative bridge.
A visa exemption does not itself state a passport-validity, funds, onward-ticket, accommodation, vaccination, fee, port or stay limit. Immigration admission and security controls remain applicable.

policies.title: Category Two ordinary passports: visa on arrival
policies.summary: The effective 24 February 2026 Department notice and its current Category Two schedule expressly allow this cohort to obtain a visa at designated ports. The portal encourages a pre-departure eVisa but preserves actual border issuance, so the easier supported route is visa_on_arrival, not evisa.
conditions: The public notice permits Category Two nationals to board without a visa and obtain one on arrival at designated ports. It does not enumerate the operating ports, an arrival fee, passport-validity, funds, onward-ticket, accommodation, vaccination, extension or stay limit; do not assume these from the separate electronic-application product.

The official PDF's phrase 'with or without prior authorization' and the portal's encouragement to apply online preserve case-specific pre-authorisation possibilities. They do not defeat the notice's expressly available arrival-issuance baseline, nor make the optional eVisa an ETA.

The notice does not establish ordinary-visitor duration or extension. Work, residence, business-only, transit, diplomatic, official, service, refugee and special-document routes are excluded; admission remains discretionary.

policies.title: Category One ordinary passports: advance electronic visa
policies.summary: The current Category One schedule requires this cohort to obtain a visa well in advance or prior authorization. The Department's live nationality selector offers its Single Entry product for each listed ordinary passport, supporting evisa rather than visa on arrival.
conditions: The source requires a visa well in advance or prior authorization. For every listed code, the live Department selector returned the electronic Single Entry product for an Ordinary Passport; this supports evisa rather than assuming a mission-only route. It does not establish any VOA alternative.

The official eVisa FAQ currently says processing is within three working days and lists electronic single-entry, transit and multiple-entry products. Its listed electronic fees include USD 50 single-entry, USD 50 transit, USD 150 six-month multiple entry and USD 250 12-month multiple entry; recheck products, fees and case processing before travel.

The eVisa is not automatic entry. It does not decide the visitor permit, stay or extension, port, passport-validity, funds, onward-ticket, accommodation, vaccination, work, residence, business-only, transit, diplomatic, official, service, refugee, special-document, security or individual-admissibility rules.

application.label: Malawi Department of Immigration eVisa portal
application.processingTime: The current official FAQ says applications are processed within three working days; apply before travel because Category One requires a visa or prior authorization before departure.
steps: Create an account and submit the applicable electronic visa application through the Department's eVisa portal.
Complete the portal's payment and provide any supporting documents or further information the Department requests.
Download and print the approved eVisa before travel, then present it for immigration examination and separate entry permission.

policies.title: Malawian citizens: constitutional right to return
policies.summary: The Constitution directly provides a right to return to the Republic, so the Malawi ordinary-passport same-country pair is not classified under a foreign visitor visa route.
conditions: This records only the constitutional return right. It does not determine passport issuance or validity, dual nationality, document screening, health, customs, criminal process, security checks or other border formalities.

policies.title: Named ordinary passports: Algeria visa-free short visit
policies.summary: The current official MFA diplomatic-post schedule expressly sets an all-non-Algerian default and names these ordinary nationalities as its visa-exempt exceptions. This is a direct nationality schedule, not a conclusion from an online application channel or from an omitted country.
conditions: The schedule names nationals, while separately listing diplomatic and official-passport exemptions. This policy is therefore limited to ordinary passport nationality and does not extend special-document privileges to other passports.

No current official source in this batch states a nationality-wide exemption duration, ports, fee, onward-ticket, accommodation, health or extension rule. Admission, public-order and security decisions remain case-specific.

The Dublin MFA mission page omits Morocco, but two separate current MFA-post schedules (Oslo and London) expressly include it in the same closed ordinary-nationality list. Morocco is assigned on that corroborated direct evidence; the unexplained Dublin omission remains a source-quality risk.
The official Grand Sud organized-tourist arrival measure and the separate Algerian-national/foreign-passport document exception are conditional routes, not ordinary passport-nationality exemptions.

Work, residence, family, medical, study, business-only, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service, refugee and stateless-document routes are outside this ordinary short-visitor baseline. The law remains subject to international agreements and reciprocity.

policies.title: All other ordinary passports: Algeria advance consular visitor visa
policies.summary: The MFA schedule expressly answers that all non-Algerians require a visa except its closed named exemption list. Combined with the central MFA instruction to obtain that visa before travel from a diplomatic or consular post, this establishes the remaining ordinary-passport complement as visa_required, not evisa or visa_on_arrival.
conditions: This is the central MFA's advance diplomatic-or-consular process. Downloadable application forms are not electronic visa issuance, and no current official source reviewed here establishes an ordinary-passport visa-on-arrival or eVisa alternative for this cohort.

The central MFA guidance requires a passport valid at least six months, travel-assistance/repatriation insurance, photos and the purpose-specific documents; tourist applicants need legalized accommodation, hotel booking or a travel-agency attestation. The competent mission is normally the applicant's place of habitual residence.

The law sets a maximum consular-visa validity of two years and a maximum stay of 90 days per entry; actual type, duration, entries, fee, grant, extension and admission remain visa- and case-specific. It also requires sufficient means and permits refusal on public-order, State-security or fundamental-interest grounds.

The official Great South measure offers an arrival regularisation visa only to foreign tourist groups travelling through an organized tourism framework, with a stay no longer than 30 days. Its route, agency and case conditions do not establish nationality-wide visa-on-arrival access.

Do not apply this passport-nationality baseline to holders of diplomatic, official, service, crew, UN or other special documents, to residents or workers, to family and other purpose-specific visas, to transit or border regularisation, or to an Algerian national travelling with a foreign passport and separate Algerian biometric passport or identity document. Those are conditional/document cases, not an ordinary foreign-passport nationality route.

application.label: Algerian Ministry of Foreign Affairs visa guidance
application.processingTime: The central guidance gives a 48-hour issuance statement only for organized tourists after the complete file reaches the competent mission; it does not promise a general processing time.
steps: Download and complete the visa form in duplicate, then gather the passport, photographs, travel insurance and purpose-specific supporting documents.
Submit the application to the Algerian Embassy or Consulate responsible for the applicant's usual residence, with the required consular fee.
Obtain the visa before travel and present the travel document and visa for border examination; a visa does not remove admissibility and security controls.

policies.title: Algerian citizens: national-passport return
policies.summary: The Interior Ministry's current national-passport guidance directly states that the document permits its holder to leave Algeria or return to it under the applicable law. The same-country ordinary-passport pair is therefore citizenship, not a foreign visitor-visa classification.
conditions: This records only the citizen return function of an Algerian national passport. It does not decide passport issuance or validity, dual nationality, identity checks, customs, health, criminal process, security screening or other border formalities.

policies.title: ECOWAS ordinary passports: Nigeria short-visit visa exemption
policies.summary: The current NIS landing-card portal labels ECOWAS passports Visa Free / Exemption, while the operative ECOWAS Protocol removes visa requirements for Community citizens visiting a Member State through an official entry point for up to 90 days. This policy maps the catalog's foreign ECOWAS ordinary passports.
conditions: The Protocol requires a valid travel document and international health certificate, limits the baseline visit to 90 days, and permits Nigeria to refuse admission to an inadmissible immigrant. It does not eliminate all border, health, security or documentary checks.

Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger formally withdrew from ECOWAS on 29 January 2025. ECOWAS's current transition notice expressly continues their visa-free movement, residence and establishment rights until further notice; their status must be rechecked if that notice changes.

This maps only ordinary passports for short visitor movement. It does not normalize ECOWAS travel certificates, residence or establishment rights, employment, transit, diplomatic, official, service, refugee or other special-document routes.
The Landing and Exit Card is an immigration declaration workflow, not an ETA or a visa. Completing it does not change this exemption.

policies.title: Category A ordinary passports: Senegal visa exemption
policies.summary: Senegal's current detailed consular schedule places these ordinary passports in Category A or its reciprocal visa-exemption arrangements. ECOWAS and temporary AES movement rules directly support the Community portion, while the schedule names the five additional ordinary-passport reciprocal exemptions.
conditions: For Community citizens, the ECOWAS Protocol requires a valid travel document and international health certificate, permits a short visit of up to 90 days through an official entry point, and preserves Senegal's right to refuse an inadmissible immigrant.

BF, ML and NE are the AES States. The current detailed Category A schedule expressly continues their visa exemption until further notice; the remaining mapped Community passports are covered by the Category A schedule.

The current consular schedule separately names CF, CG, MA, MU and TN as ordinary reciprocal visa-exemption countries. It requires a valid passport, repatriation guarantee/return or onward ticket, and health certificate as applicable.
The 2026 Foreign Ministry health notice says the vaccination card is not mandatory for entrants not arriving from epidemic/endemic-country situations; changing public-health controls may still apply.

This excludes residence, employment, study, transit, refugee status, diplomatic, service, official and mission-based document treatment. Official passports and ordinary passports on official mission have distinct conditional exemptions.

policies.title: Other foreign ordinary passports: Senegal advance consular visa
policies.summary: Senegal's current detailed consular schedule states that Category B requires a visa without mandatory Interior consultation, Category C requires prior Interior authorisation, and every passport absent from the lists follows Category C. This is an explicit complete advance-visa default, not inference from application availability.
conditions: Category B still requires a visa but has optional Interior consultation. Category C requires an authorisation of entry issued after application to the Ministry of the Interior; passports absent from all lists are expressly subject to the same Category C conditions.

The consular authority says the visa is issued by Senegalese diplomatic or consular authorities. This supports visa_required rather than evisa, visa_on_arrival or ETA; no current official source reviewed establishes a nationality-wide electronic or airport-issuance visitor alternative for this residual cohort.

Required materials vary by category but include passport validity of at least six months, visa form, photos, return/onward or repatriation evidence, accommodation and health documentation. Category C applicants are advised to apply two months in advance.

The current Foreign Ministry overview, retained from the 2015 regime, lists a materially broader visa-free cohort (including many European and other passports) than the detailed Category A/B/C page. The latter is used because it contains the post-2025 AES treatment and explicit Category C default; the conflict is a material review risk.

Work, residence, study, transit, refugee, diplomatic, official, service and official-mission exceptions are excluded. Issuance and entry remain subject to individual security, health and immigration assessment.

policies.title: Morocco: live-selector ordinary-passport visitor visa exemption
policies.summary: For these ordinary-passport tourist inputs with no additional visa and ordinary residence in the nationality country, the current Accès Maroc service returns its visa-exempt outcome, not an AEVM or visa process.
conditions: This is a current ordinary-passport tourist selector result with country of usual residence set to the nationality country and no additional visa. It does not replace different rules for residence elsewhere, a third-country visa, another purpose, event participation, diplomatic/official/special documents, refugees, stateless persons or other travel documents.

Foreign visitors remain subject to a recognized valid travel document, border examination, proof of means and purpose, and any visa where required under Law 02-03. The exemption does not guarantee admission.

The live selector was rechecked on 21 August 2026 and returns exemption for Azerbaijan, whereas the eVisa terms PDF still names Azerbaijan in Category A. The live individualized result is used, but this unresolved official-source disagreement requires maintainer confirmation.

policies.title: Morocco: ordinary-passport visitor AEVM
policies.summary: The current Accès Maroc nationality reference flags this cohort for authorization, and the portal directs it to the electronic travel-authorization process rather than visa exemption or eVisa.
conditions: AEVM is a pre-travel electronic authorization, normalized as eta. The guide separately distinguishes visa exemption, consular visa, AEVM and eVisa outcomes.

The public selector depends on nationality, ordinary passport, country of usual residence, additional visa, purpose and date of birth; this policy records only the observed nationality baseline without a qualifying third-country status.

The AEVM guide requires an account, personal/passport/travel and accommodation/financing information, supporting documents, validation and an approved downloadable authorization. It is not a visa-free route and does not guarantee admission.
Work, residence, family, transit, event, diplomatic, official, service, refugee, stateless and special-document routes are outside this policy.

application.label: Accès Maroc electronic travel authorization service
steps: Use the official eligibility form with nationality, ordinary passport, residence, any additional visa, purpose and date of birth.
If routed to AEVM, register or authenticate, complete the personal, passport and travel information, attach the required documents and validate the request.
Follow the file in the portal and download the authorization if approved before travel.

policies.title: Morocco: nationality-wide ordinary-passport eVisa
policies.summary: The current Accès Maroc service routes this named ordinary-passport tourist cohort to an eVisa without a residence permit or third-country visa condition.
conditions: The eVisa terms describe an online, single-entry visa for tourism or business, valid up to 180 days from issue for a stay not exceeding 30 days. Only ordinary passports may use it.
The application needs a passport valid at least 90 days at application, and the portal says it may be issued in 24 working hours (express) or 72 working hours (standard) for complete applications.

At the border, the eVisa holder must present the eVisa and passport and may be asked for a return ticket, means of at least EUR 70 per day and repatriation/medical insurance. Admission remains discretionary.

The eVisa terms also offer conditional routes based on an eligible residence permit or a valid multiple-entry third-country visa. Those conditions do not expand this nationality-only policy. The terms PDF names Azerbaijan as Category A but the live selector currently exempts it; Azerbaijan is therefore not included here.

application.label: Accès Maroc eVisa service
application.processingTime: The official eVisa terms state 24 working hours for express and 72 working hours for standard processing of complete applications.
steps: Check eligibility in the official Accès Maroc form and select the eVisa process.
Enter the application and attach the passport copy, photograph and purpose-specific supporting documents; validate and pay the request.
Track the file in Accès Maroc, download the approved eVisa, and present it at boarding and the Moroccan border.

policies.title: Morocco: ordinary-passport visitor consular visa baseline
policies.summary: For these ordinary-passport tourist inputs with usual residence in the nationality country and no additional visa, the live Accès Maroc service returns its visa-required outcome rather than exemption, AEVM or eVisa.
conditions: The portal's visa outcome means a Moroccan visa application is required. The official AEVM guide distinguishes this from the electronic travel authorization and eVisa outcomes, and says the visa application is lodged at the consular post.

This does not rule out the separately documented conditional eVisa paths for a traveler who holds a qualifying residence permit or an eligible valid multiple-entry third-country visa; those are not nationality-only routes.

Law 02-03 requires foreign arrivals to present a valid recognized travel document and, where applicable, an administrative visa. Visa possession does not remove border examination, evidence-of-stay or refusal risk.
This baseline excludes work, residence, family, transit, event, diplomatic, official, service, refugee, stateless and special-document treatment.

policies.title: CEMAC and Nigerian ordinary passports: Cameroon visa-free short visit
policies.summary: CEMAC’s current official material says visa-free free movement of its Member-State citizens is effective; this maps the five foreign CEMAC passports. A separate Presidency source directly supports the Cameroon–Nigeria bilateral exemption for a three-month stay. Neither source supports a visa-on-arrival or electronic-visa classification.
conditions: The CEMAC policy applies only to ordinary nationals of the five foreign Member States; it is not an extension of special, diplomatic or service-passport agreements. Admission, passport, health, security and border controls remain applicable.

The Cameroon–Nigeria bilateral source supports a stay or residence of up to three months with visa exemption. It is treated as a short-visitor exemption; its continued operation should be rechecked if the agreement or its implementing practice changes.
Do not apply this policy to employment, long-term residence, transit, diplomatic, official, service, refugee or other special-document routes.

policies.title: Other foreign ordinary passports: Cameroon online advance visa approval
policies.summary: Cameroon’s official Ministry and Prime Minister sources establish a compulsory online visa-file process for users travelling to Cameroon. MINREX says approval produces an online visa-issuance authorisation with a QR code before travel; the physical visa is then affixed at the border or competent mission. This is electronic advance approval, not an airport visa application or an ETA.
conditions: Apply through the official evisacam.cm portal before travel: create an account, enter the application, upload supporting documents, pay online and await processing by the competent diplomatic mission or consular post.

For applicants distant from a competent post, MINREX says the online QR-code visa-issuance authorisation permits travel and the visa is affixed at the entry border post. Applicants near the competent post may instead attend biometric enrolment. In both cases, approval precedes travel; the border step does not make this visa_on_arrival.

MINREX indicates normal processing within 72 hours after preregistration and express processing within 24 hours, but issuance is discretionary and individual documentary, health, security and admission requirements remain applicable.

The short-stay visa may serve temporary visitors travelling as tourists or businesspersons and cannot exceed six months. Work, study, residence, transit, family, diplomatic, official, service, courtesy, refugee and other special-document cases are separate.
The current review found no ordinary-passport nationality-wide arrival-visa cohort. The airport/border affixing mechanism is conditional on an approved online authorisation.

application.label: Cameroon official eVisa portal
application.processingTime: MINREX states 72 hours after preregistration for the normal process and 24 hours for express processing; neither guarantees grant.
steps: Create an account at the official evisacam.cm portal and complete the online visa application.
Upload the requested supporting documents and pay the required online fee.

Await the competent mission or consular post’s decision. Travel only with the issued QR-code visa-issuance authorisation, then complete visa affixing at the specified entry border post or competent mission.

policies.title: ECOWAS and AES-transition ordinary passports: Côte d’Ivoire short-visit visa exemption
policies.summary: The current ECOWAS roster identifies Côte d’Ivoire and eleven foreign current Member States. The ECOWAS Protocol provides their citizens visa-free entry for up to 90 days. Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger are no longer roster members, but ECOWAS's still-current withdrawal directive expressly continues their visa-free movement rights until further notice. This is a visa exemption, not an airport visa or electronic-visa route.
conditions: The Protocol requires a valid travel document and international health certificate, requires entry through an official point, and sets a 90-day visitor limit; a longer stay needs permission from the competent authority.

A Member State may refuse admission to a Community citizen classed as an inadmissible immigrant under its laws. Border, health, identity, security and individual-admissibility controls therefore remain applicable.

The current roster excludes BF, ML and NE following their 29 January 2025 withdrawal. ECOWAS nevertheless directs relevant authorities to continue their citizens' visa-free movement rights until further notice. Their ordinary-passport treatment is conditional on the official transition arrangement, including recognition of national passports or identity cards bearing the ECOWAS logo; it must be rechecked if ECOWAS announces final future-relation modalities.
This policy does not normalize residence, employment, diplomatic, official, service, UN laissez-passer, refugee, special-document, transit or event-specific access.

policies.title: Egypt eVisa-eligible ordinary passports: visa at port of arrival
policies.summary: Egypt's eVisa portal lists this ordinary-passport cohort for electronic applications. The Ministry of Interior's port-visa schedule says that, in addition to its separately named countries, all countries previously listed in the eVisa system receive an emergency entry visa at ports of arrival. Under the easiest-access taxonomy, the nationality-wide port route is normalized as visa_on_arrival; eVisa remains an online alternative.
conditions: The Ministry of Interior's arrival list expressly adds all countries previously listed in the eVisa system. This policy chooses the arrival-issued visa as the easier available nationality-wide route; it does not erase the official eVisa alternative.

The eVisa portal describes online issuance for tourism, single or multiple entry, and requires a passport valid at least six months from arrival, the printed eVisa, itinerary and relevant hotel or visit evidence. Border officers can refuse entry even with an eVisa.
Canada's port-arrival route is independently confirmed by the Foreign Ministry as effective from 1 December 2024; the same announcement says the eVisa option was reactivated.

Purpose-specific, work, residence, study, transit, Sinai-only, diplomatic, official, service, refugee, stateless, travel-document, security and individual-admissibility rules are outside this ordinary tourist baseline.

application.label: Egypt e-Visa Portal (optional online alternative)
steps: Use the official eVisa portal to register, supply the required traveler information and pay by credit or debit card.
Download the eVisa link sent after issuance and carry the required passport, itinerary and supporting visit or accommodation evidence.
Alternatively, use the Ministry of Interior's nationality-wide port-arrival visa route where it is the easier route in this policy.

policies.title: Additional named ordinary passports: Egypt visa at port of arrival
policies.summary: The Ministry of Interior's current port-arrival schedule expressly names this cohort in addition to eVisa-system nationalities. Each is therefore normalized as visa_on_arrival, not as an eVisa or visa-free entry.
conditions: This route is an emergency entry visa granted at ports of arrival. It is not a visa waiver, an ETA, or an inference from an online form.

The Ministry page separately qualifies Iraq by age, Belize by non-Arab origin, Guinea by occupation/funds/purpose and Turkey by non-Egyptian origin; those conditional rows are intentionally excluded from this nationality-wide policy.

Entry remains subject to purpose, duration, passport, funds, carrier, public-security and border-officer requirements. Work, residence, transit, Sinai-only, diplomatic, official, service and special-document routes are outside scope.

policies.title: Named ordinary passports: Egypt prior-visa baseline
policies.summary: The Ministry of Interior's current prior-visa schedule directly names this cohort. The six named passports that the eVisa schedule also covers are excluded because the separately documented arrival route is easier; this policy does not infer a residual default beyond the Ministry's list.
conditions: This is the ordinary-passport visitor baseline from the Ministry's named prior-visa list. It does not make an online application channel an eVisa or a tourist-arrival arrangement.

The Ministry schedule records limited exceptions based on age, sex, Egyptian family links, international-organization employment, student status, GCC marriage, Jordanian residence, an accredited tourism-company guarantee, route, occupation, ancestry or sufficient funds. Those are not nationality-wide and do not alter this baseline.

Azerbaijan, Bosnia and Herzegovina, India, Iraq, Kosovo and Vietnam appear both in the prior-visa schedule and the current eVisa schedule; they are excluded here and classified under the easier documented port-arrival route. Cambodia and Thailand remain in this policy because the current eVisa schedule does not list them.
Diplomatic, official, service, crew, residence, work, transit, Sinai-only, refugee, stateless and other special-document treatment remains outside scope.

policies.title: Mauritania: reciprocal-agreement ordinary-passport short-stay visa exemption
policies.summary: ANRPTS and the Foreign Affairs Ministry currently list reciprocal visa-suppression agreements that support ordinary-passport short visits for this 11-country foreign cohort. The ANRPTS list is used because it is the directly competent current visitor procedure; it is corroborated by the Foreign Affairs list.
conditions: The policy applies only to ordinary passports from the named reciprocal-agreement countries for a short visit. It does not extend Morocco, Syria, Yemen, the United Arab Emirates, Romania, Spain, Turkey, Brazil, China, Iran or India, whose listed agreements are limited to diplomatic, service or official passports.

ANRPTS's visitor procedure lists all eleven countries. A current APIM investment-information page lists only Algeria, Côte d’Ivoire, Gambia, Libya, Mali, Niger, Senegal and Tunisia, omitting Burkina Faso, Chad and Guinea-Bissau. The direct ANRPTS and Foreign Affairs schedules are given precedence; this unresolved official-source discrepancy requires periodic review.

The APIM summary says short stays are up to 90 days. Passport validity, border examination, security, health, purpose, work, residence, transit, diplomatic, service, UN and other special-document rules remain outside this ordinary visitor policy.

policies.title: Other foreign ordinary passports: Mauritania electronic visitor visa
policies.summary: ANRPTS states that foreign visitors may request an online entry visa, that sticker visas have been replaced by online visas, and that a validated visa is printed and used for travel. Together with its exhaustive named reciprocal-exemption list, this directly supports an eVisa baseline for every other foreign ordinary passport in the catalog.
conditions: Complete the ANRPTS online request, await validation, print the resulting eVisa for boarding, and complete biometrics at the Mauritanian point of entry. The live service offers 30-day, 90-day and 360-day packages and says electronically issued visas allow entry via all international ports of entry.

The official procedure requires a passport valid for at least six months. ANRPTS says no entry visa may be obtained with a passport under six months' validity without prior authorization from competent authorities.

Airport and border-point processing named in the government procedures portal refers to the ANRPTS procedure and biometric completion. It does not describe a nationality-wide application for a visa on arrival, so this policy remains evisa.

This policy excludes the eleven named ordinary-passport reciprocal exemptions, Mauritanian citizenship, diplomatic/service/official and UN documents, work and residence visas, transit, long-stay and individual security or admissibility decisions.

application.label: ANRPTS Mauritania eVisa application
steps: Choose the applicable visa package in the official ANRPTS service and enter passport, traveler and trip information.
Submit the online visa request and await review by the competent authority.
Print the validated eVisa for boarding and complete biometric formalities on arrival at an international port of entry.

policies.title: Foreign ordinary passports: Eritrean advance visitor visa
policies.summary: Eritrea’s current Embassy guidance expressly says a visa is required for non-Eritreans. The electronic form and online fee do not result in a wholly electronic visa: applicants must mail the original passport to the Embassy and travel only after receipt of the visa. This is an advance traditional visa requirement, not an eVisa or visa on arrival.
conditions: This policy applies to non-Eritrean holders of ordinary foreign passports. The Embassy’s National-ID exemption for Eritreans and its special official, diplomatic, family, employment, student and transit workflows are outside this ordinary foreign-visitor policy.

Choose the visa type for the actual travel purpose. Tourist and business applications require the stated online form, photo, passport validity of at least six months, residency evidence where applicable, funds or purpose evidence, fees and the stated processing period; a family visit additionally requires an Eritrean resident reference.

The online application and fee are only consular-processing steps. The Embassy requires the applicant to mail the original passport and to travel after receiving the visa, so no nationality-wide electronic issuance or airport route is established.

The categorical non-Eritrean visa rule is published by Eritrea's Washington mission, while its document-submission workflow is specific to that consular jurisdiction. No current central nationality or bilateral-exception schedule was found; travelers must use the competent Eritrean mission's workflow.

Visas are valid for three months from issue; after arrival they are typically valid for one month and may be extended or renewed through Immigration in Asmara. Entry remains subject to health, return travel, security, prior history, document and immigration controls. It grants no work, residence, internal travel permit, diplomatic, official or special-document entitlement.

application.label: Eritrean Embassy Consular Affairs Processing System
application.processingTime: Minimum 15 business days stated by the Embassy for tourist processing.
steps: Select the visit type and complete the Embassy’s online visa application and required fee.
Provide the stated photo and supporting material, including passport validity and purpose or funds evidence.
Mail the original passport to the competent Eritrean mission; travel only once the visa is received.

policies.title: Gambian ordinary passports: citizenship
policies.summary: Gambian citizenship, rather than a visitor visa category, governs the home-country entry classification. The Government Passport Office page directly describes a Gambian citizen receiving an emergency passport to travel back to The Gambia.
conditions: This is a citizenship normalization for a Gambian ordinary passport, not a rule for residence, former citizenship, nationality disputes, emergency, diplomatic, service or other special documents.

The cited Passport Office material describes return by an emergency passport after loss or destitution. Passport validity, identity, security, health, border examination and other lawful controls remain applicable.

policies.title: Current GID-listed and reconciled ordinary passports: visitor visa exemption
policies.summary: The current GID table expressly lists 17 catalog passports with visa-exemption agreements and 11 ECOWAS states with free entry. The January 2025 central Government page additionally supports Cyprus, Denmark, Ireland and Latvia, which the newer GID table does not classify. This yields 32 supported foreign catalog passports; its conflicting visa/clearance rows do not establish a further route.
conditions: The GID page’s dated country entries support the 17 agreement-listed catalog codes and 11 current ECOWAS codes. Cyprus, Denmark, Ireland and Latvia are retained only because the central Government page expressly places all EU members in its waiver category and GID gives none of those four a contrary country row.

The waiver is modelled for ordinary nationality passports only. It does not establish British Overseas Territories, Crown Dependencies, Hong Kong, Macao, refugee, stateless, emergency, diplomatic, official, service, UN, residence or other special-document treatment.

The GID exemption and ECOWAS rows do not publish an exemption-stay period. The January 2025 central Government page describes the waiver visitor context as holiday or business not exceeding 90 days; duration, passport validity, yellow-fever evidence where applicable, screening, funds/onward travel, security and final admission remain subject to GID control.

The current GID table (modified 31 October 2025) puts many other EU or Commonwealth passports in visa and/or clearance groups, while the central page says the broad categories are exempt. Those incompatible scopes are deliberately unresolved; a clearance label is not normalized as visa on arrival, eVisa or a nationality-wide advance-visa rule.

policies.title: Sudanese citizens’ constitutional right to return
policies.summary: A Sudanese citizen travelling on an ordinary Sudanese passport has a constitutional right to return; this is not a visitor-visa route for foreign nationals.
conditions: Applies to Sudanese citizens; the constitutional text states that exercise is subject to law.
Does not establish a foreign-national visa route, residence entitlement, work authorization, or exemption from security and admissibility controls.

policies.title: South Sudan: four MFA-listed visa-exempt nationalities
policies.summary: MFA’s current country-by-country visa-eligibility table marks Egypt, Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda “EXEMPTED” with zero quoted entry-visa fees. It directly supports a nationality-wide visa exemption for the listed ordinary-passport short visitor cohort, rather than a visa on arrival or electronic authorization.
conditions: The published table does not state a duration, an effective date, passport-type qualifications, permitted purpose or entry-point limitations. This normalization is limited to its explicit country-level “EXEMPTED” rows and remains subject to ordinary border, health, security, admissibility and documentary checks.

MFA says bilateral relations can affect visa treatment. Its general page separately discusses visas on arrival, embassy processing, transit visas, and diplomatic, official and service passports; none is folded into this ordinary-passport visitor exemption.

The official eVisa portal provides a downloadable electronically issued visa for approved applicants. It is not an ETA, and this policy does not require it for the four explicitly exempt nationalities.

The Trade Information Hub’s statement that “most” travellers can obtain a visa on arrival has no nationality schedule. It does not establish an arrival-visa complement or alter the explicit MFA exemptions.

Work, residence, long stays, transit, invitation or entry-permit cases, foreign South Sudanese travelling on foreign passports, diplomatic, official, service, refugee, alien and other special documents are outside this policy.

policies.title: African ordinary passports: Burkina Faso electronic short-entry visa with fee waiver
policies.summary: The Council of Ministers’ current Africa-wide fee-waiver decision expressly says the waiver is not a visa exemption. The official Embassy guidance requires online entry-visa applications and emails an eVisa for presentation at the border. This maps the catalog’s foreign ordinary passports of African states to the advance electronic short-visitor route.
conditions: The 11 September 2025 decision removes visa fees for nationals of African countries but expressly retains the visa requirement. It does not provide a visa-free ordinary-passport cohort, a duration, or a statutory exemption from normal immigration, health, security and admissibility checks.

The Embassy says that, since 1 February 2023, entry-visa applications are online; after approval, the applicant receives an email attachment labelled “EVISA” and presents it on arrival. It describes transit visas (1–5 days) and short-stay visas (1–90 days); tourism is within the short-stay visitor purpose and business, work, residence and long stay are not normalized here.

The official portal and embassy distinguish ordinary-passport electronic applications from diplomatic, service and UN laissez-passer applications. The latter, refugee, alien, emergency and other special travel documents are outside this policy.

A live National Police page says land-border and Ouagadougou-airport short visas may be issued to foreign travellers. Its stated fee is incompatible with the 2025 nationwide African fee waiver and with the newer Visa Burkina fee schedule. That page has no publication or update date and conflicts with the Embassy’s online-only wording, so it is retained as a material operational conflict rather than used to normalize an all-nationality visa_on_arrival route.

ECOWAS’s 2025 transitional statement continues visa-free movement for Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger citizens in ECOWAS states until further notice. It does not publish a reciprocal inbound ordinary-passport exemption at Burkina Faso after its withdrawal; the newer Burkina Faso Government decision controls the African visitor cohort modeled here.

A valid passport, short-visit supporting documents, a return/onward arrangement, vaccination or health documents, entry-port controls, individual decision/refusal and security checks may be required. Approval is not a guarantee of admission.

application.label: Visa Burkina electronic entry-visa service
application.processingTime: The Embassy says a successful applicant receives the eVisa email attachment after the request is accepted; no reliable current uniform processing time was published.
steps: Open the official Visa Burkina platform and register/select the appropriate transit or short-stay entry-visa route.
Submit the online application, passport and purpose/health documents, then complete any applicable online payment step; African nationals have a current visa-fee waiver.
If approved, receive the emailed EVISA document and present it with the passport at an official land or international-airport entry point.

policies.title: Guinea-Bissau: current ECOWAS Member-State citizens’ visa-free entry
policies.summary: The ECOWAS free-movement protocol gives Community citizens from the eleven other current ECOWAS Member States visa-free entry to Guinea-Bissau for a visit not exceeding 90 days.
conditions: Applies to a citizen of the named current ECOWAS Member State carrying a valid travel document issued by or on behalf of that Member State; passport code alone does not decide nationality, other travel-document categories, or dual-national document choice.

The ECOWAS Member States page retains a legacy sentence describing fifteen members, but its current named schedule and footer identify twelve. The explicit named current schedule governs this policy; Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger are handled only by the separate transition policy.
Entry must be through an official entry point with a valid travel document and international health certificate. A stay beyond 90 days requires permission from the appropriate authority.
Guinea-Bissau retains the protocol’s power to refuse admission to a Community citizen categorized as an inadmissible immigrant under its laws.

Residence, establishment, work, commercial activity, family, refugee, diplomatic, official, service, special-document, security and individual admissibility rules are not normalized by this short-visitor policy.

policies.title: Guinea-Bissau: transitional visa-free entry for Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger citizens
policies.summary: Although Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger withdrew from ECOWAS on 29 January 2025, ECOWAS directs relevant authorities to continue their citizens’ visa-free movement until further notice.
conditions: The current ECOWAS instruction is expressly transitional and applies until further notice; it must be rechecked for a subsequent ECOWAS Authority decision.

The instruction requires recognition of national passports or identity cards bearing the ECOWAS logo. This policy is limited to ordinary passports meeting that document condition and does not classify non-ECOWAS-logo, alien, refugee, emergency or other special travel documents.

The source maintains free movement, residence and establishment under ECOWAS protocols; the protocol’s official-entry-point, health-certificate, 90-day visitor extension and inadmissibility conditions remain material.

policies.title: Sierra Leone: current ECOWAS ordinary passports — visa-free entry
policies.summary: The ECOWAS Free Movement Protocol establishes visa-free entry for a Community citizen visiting another Member State for up to 90 days. The current ECOWAS roster maps its eleven foreign Member States; the eVisa terms also exclude all ECOWAS members from the electronic service.
conditions: Article 3 requires a valid travel document and international health certificate and gives a maximum 90-day stay. Immigration retains admissibility and public-order controls under the Protocol.
The current twelve-State roster excludes Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger following their withdrawal; the separately documented transitional treatment applies to Burkina Faso and Mali below.
This policy does not decide residence, work, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service, special documents, individual admissibility or any bilateral arrangement.

policies.title: Sierra Leone: Burkina Faso and Mali ordinary passports — ECOWAS transitional visa-free movement
policies.summary: Although Burkina Faso and Mali are no longer shown on ECOWAS’s current twelve-State roster, ECOWAS’s withdrawal transition instruction requires Member-State authorities to continue visa-free movement for their citizens until further notice. Sierra Leone is an ECOWAS Member State.
conditions: This is a temporary ECOWAS transition, not a current membership classification. It remains subject to a contrary later notice, ordinary admission controls, travel-document and health requirements.

The official eVisa nationality endpoints return no electronic form for Burkina Faso and Mali. That operational result is consistent with the transition but is not the legal basis for visa-free status.
It does not establish residence, work, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service or special-document treatment.

policies.title: Sierra Leone: non-ECOWAS ordinary passports — advance eVisa
policies.summary: The current official eVisa terms expressly make all countries other than ECOWAS eligible for the electronic visitor visa. This conservative policy applies only to the 87 residual passports not named in the dated 2019 visa-on-arrival announcement; it does not rank the current route for that historic cohort.
conditions: The terms call eVisa a multi-entry electronic travel authorization, send an approved eVisa by email and require a copy at first arrival. It is a genuine advance eVisa, not merely an online form or an optional registration. Legacy portal UI wording about visa issuance at the terminal is inconsistent and should be rechecked, but does not erase the required prior electronic application and emailed approval.

The eVisa is for tourist and business purposes only, valid for one year from issue, normally multiple entry, with a maximum three-month stay and no extension. Passport must have at least six months remaining at entry; all airports and seaports are stated ports.

Biometrics are captured on arrival; funds, health, security, border examination and other entry conditions apply. The eVisa does not authorize paid employment, residence, study, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service or special-document travel.

Burkina Faso and Mali are excluded here under the current ECOWAS transition; their live official selector has no forms. The dated 2019 visa-on-arrival cohort is deliberately not assigned a current status or route ranking in this policy.

application.label: Sierra Leone Immigration Department eVisa service
application.processingTime: Not established by the reviewed current official terms.
steps: Use the official eVisa portal and select nationality and visa type.
Submit the electronic visa application and payment; approval is notified by email.
Carry the approved eVisa and the same valid passport at arrival for Immigration examination and biometric capture.

policies.title: Foreign EAC ordinary passports: Burundi visa-free short-visitor entry
policies.summary: Current EAC sources identify the seven other Partner States and state that all Partner States implement visa-free entry for Partner-State citizens. This maps the seven foreign EAC passport codes to Burundi visa-free entry. Burundi Tourism separately says all foreigners need a visa except EAC citizens, but its parenthetical list omits Somalia; the current EAC sources control that new Partner-State mapping.
conditions: Applies only to citizens holding ordinary passports of the seven other current EAC Partner States: Democratic Republic of the Congo, Kenya, Rwanda, Somalia, South Sudan, Tanzania and Uganda.

The EAC free-movement guarantee remains subject to host-State public-policy, public-security, public-health, border-document and individual-admissibility controls; it is not a work, residence, refugee, diplomatic, official, service, crew or special-document classification.

CGM describes a free EAC access visa issued for up to six months and says it does not grant a right to work. This post-entry administrative status does not turn the entry rule into a visa-on-arrival requirement.

Burundi Tourism’s current page calls EAC the exception but names only Kenya, Uganda, DRC, Rwanda, Tanzania and South Sudan. Somalia is retained under the current EAC Partner-State and all-Partner-State implementation evidence; this source discrepancy should be rechecked.

policies.title: Other foreign ordinary passports: Burundi simple entry visa at Melchior Ndadaye International Airport
policies.summary: Burundi Tourism’s current visitor guidance expressly requires a visa for every foreigner other than EAC citizens. The directly competent CGM says its simple entry visa for a foreign citizen is obtained online, at Melchior Ndadaye International Airport or at embassies. Because the same nationality-wide route is available at the airport, it is normalized as visa_on_arrival; the online application is an alternative channel, not a mandatory eVisa.
conditions: The simple entry visa allows a foreign citizen one entry and a one-month stay. Its airport route is expressly limited to Melchior Ndadaye International Airport; it does not establish visa issuance at every land or other air border.

The CGM portal also offers online application and embassy processing. Those alternative channels do not replace the explicitly available airport-issued route in the easiest-access taxonomy, and the portal’s online certificate/application process is not normalized as an eVisa.

The CGM airport form requests identity, ordinary travel-document, arrival, accommodation, contact and supporting information. Visa issuance and admission remain subject to purpose, documentation, health, security and border discretion.

The policy excludes Burundi citizenship, the seven foreign EAC citizen exemptions, work, study, establishment, permanent residence, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service, refugee and special-document routes. CGM separately displays free CEPGL and EAC entry-visa administrative categories; the latter does not change the EAC exemption, while no current membership-and-entry instrument is used to give Congo a different nationality status from its otherwise supported airport route.

Burundi Tourism lists a 70 USD per-month entry-visa charge, while CGM presents different fees for other entry categories and does not display an airport-form price. No fee is normalized; the direct airport issuance channel, not a price, is the basis for visa_on_arrival.
